title: Agasthyakoodam Trek
shortDescription: A sacred biosphere peak in southern Kerala, open for only a few weeks each year.
description: Agasthyakoodam rises to 6,129 ft in the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, and it is one of the most tightly controlled treks in India: a short seasonal window, a fixed daily quota allotted by online lottery, and a mandatory forest department escort. The forest holds a remarkable concentration of medicinal plants and endemic species. The peak is sacred to the sage Agastya, and the Kani community regards the whole range as holy.
bestSeason: January to March, subject to the annual permit window

itinerary.description: A long rainforest walk with river crossings to the forest department base camp.

title: Ala Kul Trek
shortDescription: A turquoise glacial lake in the Kyrgyz Tien Shan, reached over a high scree pass.
description: Ala Kul is a glacial lake at around 11,500 ft in the Terskey Alatau range above Karakol, its water an intense turquoise that shifts with the light. The trek from Karakol climbs through spruce forest and the Karakol valley, crosses the Ala Kul pass at close to 12,800 ft on loose scree, and descends to the Altyn Arashan hot springs. Wild camping is unrestricted, the valleys hold shepherd yurts, and the season is short.

itinerary.description: Walk up the Karakol valley through spruce forest.

itinerary.description: A day at the springs with side walks up the valley.

itinerary.title: Altyn Arashan to Karakol
itinerary.description: Walk or drive out the rough valley track.

title: Alang Madan Kulang Trek
shortDescription: The hardest trek in the Sahyadri — three fort summits linked by rope-assisted rock patches.
description: AMK is the benchmark for difficulty in Maharashtra. The three forts of Alang, Madan and Kulang sit in a row in the Kalsubai range, and linking them means several sections of exposed rock climbing where fixed ropes and harnesses are standard, along with rock-cut steps that have partly crumbled. It takes three days, there is no water on the traverse sections, and it should only be attempted with an experienced team and proper gear.

itinerary.description: A steep approach and the rope-assisted rock patch onto Alang, camping in the summit caves.

itinerary.description: The final and hardest traverse to Kulang, then a long descent to the village.

title: Ali Bedni Bugyal Trek
shortDescription: The twin meadows of the Roopkund trail, walked as a destination in their own right.
description: Ali and Bedni are the two largest high-altitude meadows in Uttarakhand, sitting side by side at around 11,500 ft with Trishul and Nanda Ghunti directly above them. Since access to Roopkund itself was restricted, the meadows have become the trek rather than the waypoint — and they hold up entirely, with rolling grassland that runs for kilometres, the small Bedni Kund shrine, and forest camps at Didna and Gehroli Patal on the way.
bestSeason: December to April, September to November

title: Amarkantak River Trail Trek
shortDescription: Walking from the source of the Narmada across the Maikal hills.
description: Amarkantak is where the Narmada rises, on a plateau in the Maikal range that also gives birth to the Son and the Johila. The walking here follows sal forest trails between the source temple, the Kapildhara falls and tribal villages, with the Achanakmar tiger reserve nearby. It is gentle terrain at around 3,500 ft, and the interest is as much in the pilgrimage geography and the forest as in any climbing.

itinerary.description: Walk from the source temple through sal forest to the waterfall.

title: Anamudi Trek
shortDescription: The highest peak in India south of the Himalaya, inside Eravikulam National Park.
description: Anamudi is the tallest mountain in South India at 8,842 ft, standing at the centre of Eravikulam National Park, which protects the world's largest surviving population of Nilgiri tahr. Because it lies in the park's core zone, general trekking to the summit is not permitted; public access is limited to the Rajamalai tourism zone at the base. Any climb requires special research or conservation permission from the Kerala Forest Department.
bestSeason: Restricted — core zone closed to general trekking

itinerary.title: Rajamalai zone and the Anamudi base
itinerary.description: The public trail through the Rajamalai tourism zone below the peak; the summit itself lies in the closed core zone and needs special permission.

title: Andharban Trek
shortDescription: The dark forest — a descending monsoon trek from Pimpri dam down into the Konkan.
description: Andharban means dark forest, and the canopy over this trail is thick enough that little light reaches the path even at midday. Unusually for the Sahyadri, the route descends rather than climbs: from the Pimpri dam near Tamhini it drops steadily through evergreen forest to Bhira in the Konkan, past waterfalls, streams and viewpoints over the Kundalika valley. It is at its best in the monsoon when the whole forest runs with water.

itinerary.title: Pimpri Dam to Bhira
itinerary.description: A day-long descent through dense evergreen forest, past waterfalls and Konkan viewpoints, to the Bhira powerhouse village.

title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
shortDescription: Into the Annapurna Sanctuary, a glacial amphitheatre ringed by peaks on every side.
description: The Annapurna Base Camp trek climbs from Nayapul through Ghandruk and the Modi Khola gorge into the Annapurna Sanctuary, a natural amphitheatre where Annapurna I, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre and Gangapurna form an almost complete ring around the camp at 13,550 ft. It is shorter and lower than Everest Base Camp, runs on teahouses throughout, and passes through rhododendron forest that flowers spectacularly in spring.
bestSeason: March to May, October to November

title: Ayodhya Hills Trek
shortDescription: A rocky plateau in Purulia, at its best when the palash forest flowers red in spring.
description: The Ayodhya Hills are an extension of the Eastern Ghats into Purulia district, a plateau of granite outcrops, dry forest and small dams. In February and March the palash — flame of the forest — blooms across the hillsides and turns the landscape orange-red. Trails link Bamni and Turga falls, the Marble Lake quarry pool and the plateau villages, on easy terrain that suits a winter or spring weekend.

itinerary.description: Walk the plateau trails between the two waterfalls through palash and sal forest.

title: Bagini Glacier Trek
shortDescription: Into the Nanda Devi outer sanctuary, below the Changabang and Kalanka wall.
description: The Bagini glacier lies in the outer Nanda Devi sanctuary above Jumma village, and the trek to it puts you directly beneath Changabang, Kalanka and Trishuli — some of the most technically famous rock in the Himalaya. The route through Dronagiri village is steep and the upper camps sit on moraine. Advance base camp at around 15,000 ft was the staging point for several historic expeditions. Permits from the Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve are required.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October

title: Bali Pass Trek
shortDescription: A hard crossing from the Har Ki Dun valley over to Yamunotri, with a steep snow descent.
description: Bali Pass links two of Garhwal's great valleys and asks a lot in return. The approach runs past Ruinsara Tal, an alpine lake below Swargarohini, before a long climb to a camp at Odari and a summit-day crossing of the 16,240 ft pass. The descent on the Yamunotri side is steep, sustained and often on snow, which is what pushes this into serious territory. Prior high-altitude experience is genuinely necessary.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October

title: Ballalarayana Durga to Bandaje Falls Trek
shortDescription: A ridge traverse from a ruined hill fort to the top of a 200-foot waterfall.
description: This traverse links the ruins of Ballalarayana Durga, a Hoysala-era fort above Sunkasale, with the top of Bandaje Arbi, a waterfall that drops roughly 200 feet off the edge of the plateau. Between them is a long walk across open grassland ridges with almost no shade and no reliable water, ending in a steep descent to Ujire. It is one of the finest ridge walks in Karnataka and needs forest department permission.
location: Chikkamagaluru to Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka, India

itinerary.title: Sunkasale to Ballalarayana Durga and the ridge camp
itinerary.description: Climb to the fort ruins and walk the grassland ridge to a camp near the plateau edge.

itinerary.title: Bandaje Falls and descent to Ujire
itinerary.description: Reach the top of the falls, then take the long steep descent off the plateau.

title: Banasura Hill Trek
shortDescription: Wayanad's second-highest peak, overlooking the largest earth dam in India.
description: Banasura Hill rises to 6,758 ft above the Banasura Sagar reservoir, the largest earth dam in India and the second-largest in Asia. The trek from Meenmutty or Thariode climbs through coffee plantation and shola forest to open grassland, with the reservoir and its scattered islands laid out below. Mist rolls across the summit for much of the year and the wind on the ridge is constant. Forest permits apply.

itinerary.title: Thariode to Banasura Hill and back
itinerary.description: Climb through plantation and shola into grassland for the reservoir view from the summit, then descend.

title: Beas Kund Trek
shortDescription: To the glacial source of the Beas, ringed by the mountaineering peaks of the Solang valley.
description: Beas Kund is the small glacial lake where the Beas river begins, tucked at the head of the Solang valley. The trek is short and popular as a first Himalayan outing, but the setting is serious: Hanuman Tibba, Friendship Peak, Shitidhar and Ladakhi Peak stand in a semicircle around the campsite at Dhundi and Bakarthach. Most groups do it in four days with a rest at Bakarthach, and it doubles as the standard approach for Friendship Peak attempts.

title: Bhimashankar Trek
shortDescription: A jyotirlinga temple at the top of a wildlife sanctuary, reached by the Shidi or Ganesh ghat.
description: Bhimashankar is one of the twelve jyotirlingas and also a wildlife sanctuary protecting the Indian giant squirrel, Maharashtra's state animal. Two trails climb to it from Khandas: the Ganesh Ghat, long and gradual, and the Shidi Ghat, shorter and steeper with iron ladders bolted across rock faces. Both pass through thick evergreen forest that stays green through the dry months. The Nagphani viewpoint above the temple looks out over the whole Konkan.

itinerary.description: Climb the ladder route through dense sanctuary forest to the temple plateau.

itinerary.title: Nagphani viewpoint and descend via Ganesh Ghat
itinerary.description: Walk to the Konkan Kada viewpoint at Nagphani, then take the gentler ghat down.

title: Bhrigu Lake Trek
shortDescription: Above the treeline from day one — a short trek that spends almost all of it in open meadow.
description: Bhrigu Lake is unusual in that you gain the alpine zone almost immediately. From Gulaba the trail climbs straight into rolling meadows and stays there, giving three days of uninterrupted views across the Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal. The lake itself sits at 14,100 ft in a bowl below the ridgeline, held sacred to the sage Bhrigu and frozen for much of the year. It is one of the best short high-altitude treks in Himachal.

itinerary.description: A steep climb to the lake bowl, then the full descent to the road.

itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Bodpathri Trek
shortDescription: A little-walked meadow and lake circuit in the Pir Panjal above Yusmarg.
description: Bodpathri is a wide meadow and small alpine lake in the Pir Panjal range west of Srinagar, reached from the shepherd country above Yusmarg or Doodhpatri. It gets a fraction of the traffic of the Lidder-side treks, and the walking is through rolling grassland, conifer forest and Gujjar summer settlements. A short trek that works well as an introduction to Kashmir before attempting the bigger lake routes.

title: Brahmagiri Peak Trek
shortDescription: A wildlife sanctuary climb from Iruppu Falls to the Karnataka-Kerala ridge.
description: The Brahmagiri range straddles the Coorg-Wayanad border, and the trek starts at the Iruppu Falls before climbing through the wildlife sanctuary into shola forest and grassland. The Munikal cave sits partway up, and the summit ridge at 5,276 ft looks down into Kerala on one side and Kodagu on the other. Forest department permits are compulsory, group sizes are limited and elephants are regularly present on the lower trail.

itinerary.description: Climb past the falls and Munikal cave through sanctuary forest to the grassland ridge, then return within permit hours.

title: Brahmatal Trek
shortDescription: A winter ridge walk with Trishul and Nanda Ghunti in view for most of it.
description: Brahmatal gives you a high-altitude winter trek with a genuinely big mountain view without the commitment of Roopkund. From Lohajung the trail climbs through oak and rhododendron to a frozen lake, then onto a long open ridge where Trishul and Nanda Ghunti sit almost close enough to touch. Deep snow from January to March makes it one of the better winter options in Garhwal, and the summit at Brahmatal Top is a straightforward walk-up.

title: Buran Ghati Trek
shortDescription: A rappel off a snow wall to finish a pass crossing between Shimla and Kinnaur.
description: Buran Ghati packs meadows, a forest lake, a hanging valley and a genuinely thrilling finish into eight days. The route from Janglik climbs past Dayara meadow and the Chandranahan lake basin to a 15,000 ft pass, and the descent on the far side goes over a steep snow wall that most groups rappel with a fixed rope. Below it the trail drops into the Barua valley and the apple country of Kinnaur.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October
location: Shimla to Kinnaur, Himachal Pradesh, India

title: Chadar Trek
shortDescription: Walking the frozen Zanskar river in the depths of a Ladakhi winter.
description: The Chadar is the sheet of ice that forms over the Zanskar river each January and February, and for generations it was the only winter link between Zanskar and Leh. Walking it means sliding along ice over running water in temperatures that fall to minus thirty at night, camping in caves along the gorge walls. Access is regulated by the Ladakh administration with mandatory medical clearance and a permit; conditions vary year to year and the ice is never guaranteed.

title: Chembra Peak Trek
shortDescription: Wayanad's highest peak, with a heart-shaped lake that has reportedly never dried up.
description: Chembra is the tallest peak in Wayanad at 6,890 ft, climbed through tea estates and grassland from Meppadi. Partway up is Hridayasarass, a small natural lake shaped almost exactly like a heart, which local lore holds has never gone dry. Access is controlled by the forest department with a daily cap, mandatory guides and timing restrictions, and the summit section has been closed at various times after fire damage — check before travelling.

title: Churdhar Peak Trek
shortDescription: The highest point in the outer Himalaya of Himachal, with a Shirgul Devta shrine on top.
description: Churdhar is the tallest peak in the Sirmaur region at 11,965 ft, and because it stands clear of the ranges around it the summit view is exceptional — the Gangetic plain on one side, the Badrinath and Kinner Kailash peaks on the other. The trail from Nohradhar climbs through thick deodar to a summit crowned by a statue of Shirgul Devta. It is a short, steep trek, popular in summer and challenging under winter snow.
bestSeason: April to June, September to November

title: Dafeybhir Pass Trek
shortDescription: A quiet West Sikkim pass through moss forest and high lakes, named for the Himalayan monal.
description: Dafeybhir takes its name from the dafey, the Himalayan monal pheasant, which is often seen along the trail. The route from Uttarey climbs through some of the mossiest, most primeval forest in Sikkim to Chiwabhanjyang on the Nepal border, then over the pass at around 13,600 ft past a chain of small alpine lakes. It is far less trafficked than Goechala and gives a similar Kanchenjunga skyline from a different angle.
bestSeason: March to May, October to November

title: David Scott Trail Trek
shortDescription: A 16 km stretch of a colonial-era horse-cart route through the Khasi hills.
description: The David Scott Trail is the surviving walkable section of a 19th-century route built between Assam and Bangladesh, named for the British administrator who commissioned it. The walk from Mawphlang to Ladmawphlang crosses grassland ridges, pine stands, a river with a small waterfall, and Khasi villages with monoliths standing in the fields. It is a single-day walk on gentle ground and one of the best introductions to Meghalaya.

itinerary.description: A full day's walk from the sacred grove at Mawphlang across grassland ridges, river crossings and Khasi hamlets to the far trailhead.

title: Dayara Bugyal Trek
shortDescription: One of the largest and most gently rolling alpine meadows in the country.
description: Dayara is a meadow trek in the purest sense: an enormous, almost absurdly smooth grassland at 11,000 ft, folded into low hills, with Bandarpoonch and Draupadi Ka Danda ranged along the skyline. The climb from Raithal is short, which makes it a strong first Himalayan trek and an easy winter one, when the whole bugyal turns into an unbroken snowfield. Barnala Tal on the way up is a good acclimatisation stop.
bestSeason: December to April, September to November

title: Debrigarh Sanctuary Trek
shortDescription: Dry deciduous forest along the Hirakud reservoir, with bison and a rebel fort in the hills.
description: Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary spreads along the northern edge of the Hirakud reservoir in western Odisha, a dry deciduous forest with a large gaur population and the hill fort where Veer Surendra Sai sheltered during his rebellion against the British. Trails run between the reservoir shore, the Debrigarh hill and the grasslands, and winter brings large numbers of migratory waterbirds to the water's edge.

itinerary.title: Dhodrokusum to the reservoir camp
itinerary.description: Walk the forest track to a camp on the Hirakud shore.

itinerary.title: Debrigarh hill and the fort site
itinerary.description: Climb to the hill and the historic rebel stronghold with views over the water.

itinerary.title: Grassland trails and exit
itinerary.description: A last morning among the grasslands and back to the gate.

title: Deoriatal Chandrashila Trek
shortDescription: A reflecting lake, a rhododendron forest and a summit above the highest Shiva temple in the world.
description: This trek packs an unusual amount into a short route. It starts at Deoriatal, a still lake that holds a perfect reflection of Chaukhamba at sunrise, crosses ridgelines thick with rhododendron, and finishes on Chandrashila at 12,083 ft, just above Tungnath — the highest of the Panch Kedar temples. The summit view runs from Nanda Devi through Trishul, Kedar Dome and Chaukhamba. April brings the rhododendron bloom; winter brings snow to the summit ridge.
bestSeason: December to April, September to November

itinerary.description: Drive up the Mandakini valley to the base village of Sari.

itinerary.title: Sari to Deoriatal
itinerary.description: A short steep climb to the lake, camping beside it for the Chaukhamba reflection at dawn.

itinerary.title: Deoriatal to Baniyakund
itinerary.description: A long ridge traverse through Rohini Bugyal and rhododendron forest.

itinerary.title: Baniyakund to Chandrashila summit and back to Chopta
itinerary.description: Climb past Tungnath temple to the summit, then descend to the Chopta roadhead.

itinerary.title: Chopta to Rishikesh
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Devkund Waterfall Trek
shortDescription: A short forest walk to a plunge pool where three streams fall into one turquoise basin.
description: Devkund sits at the origin of the Kundalika river near Bhira, where three separate falls drop into a single deep pool the colour of jade. The walk in from Bhira village is around three kilometres through forest and across streams, easy in itself but slippery in heavy rain. Swimming is restricted and life jackets are compulsory — the pool is deep and there have been drownings. Local guides are mandatory and the trail closes in severe weather.

itinerary.title: Bhira Village to Devkund and back
itinerary.description: A forest and stream walk to the plunge pool, time at the falls, and the return on the same trail.

title: Dodital Darwa Top Trek
shortDescription: A trout lake in deep forest, with a ridge above it looking at Bandarpoonch.
description: Dodital is a freshwater lake at around 10,000 ft ringed by oak, deodar and rhododendron, regarded in local tradition as the birthplace of Ganesha and stocked with Himalayan trout. Above it, Darwa Top opens onto a ridge with Bandarpoonch, Swargarohini and the Gangotri group in view. The trek from Sangamchatti is a forest walk for most of its length, which makes it a good all-season option and pleasant in light snow.
bestSeason: April to June, September to November

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Sangamchatti
itinerary.description: Drive via Uttarkashi to the trailhead.

itinerary.title: Sangamchatti to Bebra
itinerary.description: A forest walk along the Asi Ganga.

itinerary.title: Bebra to Dodital
itinerary.description: Climb through deodar and oak to the lake and its Ganesha temple.

itinerary.title: Dodital to Darwa Top and back
itinerary.description: A ridge climb for the Bandarpoonch panorama, then return to the lake.

itinerary.title: Dodital to Sangamchatti
itinerary.description: Descend the forest trail to the roadhead.

title: Doodhpatri Trek
shortDescription: The valley of milk — gentle grassland walking an hour and a half from Srinagar.
description: Doodhpatri takes its name from the milky white of the stream that runs through it, foaming over stones across a floor of soft grass. The walking here is easy and rolling, through meadow and pine with the Pir Panjal on the horizon, and Gujjar and Bakarwal shepherd families camped through the summer. It suits families and first-time trekkers, and works as a snow-walking destination in winter.

itinerary.title: Srinagar to Doodhpatri, trek to Tangnar
itinerary.description: Drive out of the city and walk up the meadow to a stream-side camp.

itinerary.title: Tangnar to Doodhpatri and Srinagar
itinerary.description: An easy walk back down and return drive.

title: Dudhsagar Waterfall Trek
shortDescription: A four-tiered fall on the Mandovi, crossed by a railway bridge halfway down.
description: Dudhsagar means sea of milk, and the fall drops around 310 metres in four tiers on the Goa-Karnataka border inside the Bhagwan Mahaveer sanctuary. The railway line to Castle Rock crosses its face, which produced the well-known image of a train passing in front of the water. Walking the tracks is prohibited and enforced; the legal routes are the jeep safari from Kulem or trekking approaches from Castle Rock organised with forest permits.
location: South Goa and Belagavi, Goa and Karnataka, India

itinerary.title: Kulem to Dudhsagar Falls and back
itinerary.description: Enter the sanctuary with permits, reach the base of the falls, and return the same day.

title: Dzongri Trek
shortDescription: The shorter half of the Goechala route, for the Dzongri Top sunrise alone.
description: Dzongri is the great meadow camp on the Kanchenjunga approach, and for trekkers without ten days to spare it works perfectly as a destination in its own right. The route from Yuksom is the same demanding rhododendron climb through Sachen and Tshoka, and the reward is the same dawn on Dzongri Top, with Kanchenjunga, Pandim, Kabru and Rathong catching light in sequence. Five to six days, with all the character of the longer trek.
bestSeason: March to May, October to November

itinerary.title: Bagdogra to Yuksom
itinerary.description: Drive into West Sikkim.

itinerary.title: Yuksom to Sachen
itinerary.description: Enter the national park on the forest trail.

itinerary.title: Sachen to Tshoka
itinerary.description: Cross the Prek Chu and climb to the village.

itinerary.title: Tshoka to Dzongri
itinerary.description: The steep rhododendron climb to the meadow.

itinerary.title: Dzongri Top and descend to Tshoka
itinerary.description: Dawn on Dzongri Top, then the long descent.

itinerary.title: Tshoka to Yuksom
itinerary.description: Walk out to the roadhead.

title: Dzukou Valley Trek
shortDescription: A valley of rolling green bamboo on the Nagaland-Manipur border, home to the Dzukou lily.
description: Dzukou is unlike anything else in India: a high valley floor covered in a dense, uniform dwarf bamboo that makes the hills look upholstered, cut through by a stream that freezes in winter. The endemic Dzukou lily blooms from June to September. The trek is short — a steep climb from Viswema or the gentler Zakhama route to a rest house, then wandering the valley itself. Rock caves serve as shelter and the nights get genuinely cold.
bestSeason: June to September, December to February

itinerary.title: Kohima to Viswema, trek to Dzukou rest house
itinerary.description: Drive to the trailhead and take the steep direct climb to the valley rim.

itinerary.title: Explore the valley
itinerary.description: Walk the valley floor and stream, and up to the ridge for the full view.

itinerary.title: Descend via Zakhama to Kohima
itinerary.description: Take the longer, gentler trail out and return to Kohima.

title: Ettina Bhuja Trek
shortDescription: The ox's shoulder — a short grassland climb with an outsized view of the Charmadi range.
description: Ettina Bhuja is named for a rock formation that resembles an ox's shoulder, and it delivers a disproportionate view for a short walk: the whole Charmadi ghat, Amedikallu and Ombattu Gudda spread out from a small summit with a Durga shrine. The trail from Byrapura is about three kilometres of steady grassland climbing. Ideal as a half-day trek or paired with Amedikallu across a weekend.

itinerary.title: Byrapura to Ettina Bhuja and back
itinerary.description: A steady grassland climb to the shrine on the summit rock and the descent by the same trail.

title: Everest Base Camp Trek
shortDescription: The Khumbu classic — Namche, Tengboche and Kala Patthar at 18,519 ft.
description: The trek to Everest Base Camp runs through the Khumbu from Lukla, climbing past Namche Bazaar, the Tengboche monastery and the Sherpa villages of Dingboche and Lobuche to the Khumbu glacier. Base camp itself sits at 17,598 ft, and most itineraries add Kala Patthar at 18,519 ft for the clearest view of Everest's summit pyramid. It is a teahouse trek throughout; altitude, not terrain, is the difficulty.
bestSeason: March to May, September to November

itinerary.description: Fly into Lukla and walk down the Dudh Koshi valley.

itinerary.title: Phakding to Namche Bazaar

itinerary.title: Namche to Tengboche

itinerary.title: Tengboche to Dingboche
itinerary.description: Above the treeline into the Imja valley.

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation in Dingboche
itinerary.description: Climb Nangkartshang ridge for height gain.

itinerary.title: Dingboche to Lobuche
itinerary.description: Past the Thukla memorials onto the Khumbu glacier moraine.

itinerary.title: Lobuche to Gorak Shep and Base Camp
itinerary.description: Moraine walking to the base camp site below the Khumbu icefall.

title: Gaumukh Tapovan Trek
shortDescription: To the snout of the Gangotri glacier and the meadow that sits directly beneath Shivling.
description: Gaumukh is where the Bhagirathi emerges from the Gangotri glacier, and the trek there is a walk up the moraine of one of the largest glacier systems in the Himalaya. Beyond it, a steep and genuinely exposed climb onto the glacier's true left leads to Tapovan, a high meadow with sadhus' caves and an uninterrupted face-on view of Shivling. Permits from the Gangotri National Park are compulsory and capped daily.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October

itinerary.description: Drive along the Bhagirathi to Uttarkashi.

itinerary.title: Uttarkashi to Gangotri

itinerary.description: A long walk through the national park along the Bhagirathi gorge.

itinerary.description: Walk out along the gorge trail.

itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Gidara Bugyal Trek
shortDescription: A vast, almost unvisited meadow said to be among the largest in the Himalaya.
description: Gidara is a high grassland above the Bhagirathi valley that runs for kilometres in every direction, at a scale that makes even Dayara look modest. It was closed to trekking for years and reopened only recently, so it remains quiet. The approach from Bhangeli climbs steeply into the meadow, and the walking on top is long, open and exposed with Gangotri and Bandarpoonch peaks along the skyline.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October

itinerary.description: Drive up the Bhagirathi valley to the base village.

itinerary.description: Walk into the main meadow, with the range opening on all sides.

itinerary.description: A long day across the meadow towards the Dayara side.

itinerary.description: Drop through Dayara Bugyal and the forest to the village.

itinerary.title: Raithal to Dehradun
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Girnar Trek
shortDescription: Around ten thousand stone steps to a cluster of Jain and Hindu temples on five summits.
description: Girnar near Junagadh is a volcanic massif with roughly 10,000 stone steps climbing to five successive summits, each carrying temples — a major Jain pilgrimage site with 12th-century marble temples on the first peak, and the Dattatreya and Kalika shrines higher up. It is a hard stair climb rather than a technical one, usually started well before dawn to beat the heat, and the surrounding forest is part of the Gir lion habitat.

itinerary.title: Junagadh to Girnar summits and back
itinerary.description: A pre-dawn start up the stone steps through the Jain temple complex to Ambaji, Gorakhnath and Dattatreya peaks, then the descent.

title: Goechala Trek
shortDescription: The closest a trekker can legally stand to Kanchenjunga, with fourteen major peaks in one view.
description: Goechala is a pass on the southeast approach to Kanchenjunga, and the reason people walk ten days for it is the sunrise at Dzongri Top and View Point 1, where the world's third-highest mountain fills the sky at close range along with Pandim, Kabru and a dozen others. The route through the Khangchendzonga National Park passes rhododendron forest, the Prek Chu gorge and the meadow camps at Dzongri and Thansing. Permits are required and access beyond View Point 1 is restricted.
bestSeason: March to May, September to November

itinerary.description: A long drive into West Sikkim to the historic first capital.

itinerary.title: Sachen to Tshoka
itinerary.description: Cross the Prek Chu bridges and climb steeply to a Tibetan settlement village.

itinerary.title: Tshoka to Dzongri
itinerary.description: A hard climb through dense rhododendron to the meadow at Dzongri.

title: Gokarna Coastal Trek
shortDescription: Five beaches linked by clifftop paths along the Karnataka coast.
description: The Gokarna coastal walk strings together Kudle, Om, Half Moon, Paradise and Belekan beaches on a trail that climbs over headlands between each one. The walking is short but the clifftop sections are exposed and the laterite gets slippery when wet. Camping on the beaches, swimming between the headlands and the temple town of Gokarna itself make it a good winter weekend, and it works as a beginner trek with a genuinely different landscape.

itinerary.title: Half Moon to Belekan
itinerary.description: Continue along the cliffs past Paradise Beach to the fishing village at Belekan.

title: Green Lake Trek
shortDescription: The Zemu glacier approach to Kanchenjunga's north face — a restricted, expedition-grade route.
description: Green Lake sits at the head of the Zemu glacier in North Sikkim, directly beneath the north face of Kanchenjunga, and it was the base for several historic attempts on the mountain. The trek from Lachen is long, wet and remote, following the Zemu Chu through dense forest and moraine with very little infrastructure. It falls in a protected and militarily sensitive zone, so a Protected Area Permit through a registered operator is mandatory and approvals are not guaranteed.
bestSeason: April to May, October to November

itinerary.description: Drive north through the Teesta valley.

itinerary.title: Lachen to Jakthang
itinerary.description: Enter the Khangchendzonga reserve on a humid forest trail.

itinerary.title: Jakthang to Yabuk
itinerary.description: Climb along the Zemu Chu through rhododendron and bamboo.

title: Gurez Valley Trek
shortDescription: A trek through the Dard-Shin villages of the Kishanganga valley, close to the Line of Control.
description: Gurez sits on the far side of the Razdan Pass in the Kishanganga valley, a place of log-built houses, Dard-Shin communities and the distinctive pyramid of Habba Khatoon peak. Trekking here is as much about the villages and the culture as the mountains, walking between hamlets like Tulail and Bagtore through meadows and along the river. Permits and identity documents are required given the proximity to the Line of Control.

itinerary.description: Drive over the pass into the Kishanganga valley.

itinerary.description: Climb into the grazing meadows above the valley.

itinerary.title: Chakwali to Patalwan
itinerary.description: A high traverse with views towards Habba Khatoon and the Tulail side.

itinerary.description: Descend into the Tulail valley and its villages.

title: Guru Ghasidas Jungle Trek
shortDescription: Sal forest and sandstone plateaus in one of central India's least-visited national parks.
description: Guru Ghasidas National Park in northern Chhattisgarh is a large tract of sal forest, grassland and sandstone escarpment that sees very few visitors, and which has been considered for reintroduction of large carnivores. Trekking here means forest tracks, plateau edges and stream crossings, with sloth bear, gaur and a rich bird list. Access is through the forest department with guides, and the season is limited to the cooler dry months.

itinerary.title: Walk out to Sonhat

title: Hampta Pass Trek
shortDescription: A crossover trek where green Kullu turns into barren Lahaul in the space of a single descent.
description: Hampta Pass is the clearest demonstration in the Indian Himalaya of what a mountain range does to weather. The Kullu side is all pine forest, wildflowers and the rushing Rani nala; you climb to a narrow 14,065 ft notch, drop over it, and land in Lahaul's dry, brown, almost lunar Chandra valley. Most itineraries add a drive to Chandratal at the end. The pass day involves a steep snow descent that stays interesting well into the season.
location: Kullu and Lahaul, Himachal Pradesh, India

itinerary.description: Reach Manali and acclimatise.

itinerary.description: Drive to Jobra and walk into the Rani nala valley through maple and silver birch.

title: Har Ki Dun Trek
shortDescription: A cradle-shaped valley below Swargarohini, walked through some of the oldest villages in the Himalaya.
description: Har Ki Dun is a valley trek rather than a summit chase, and its pleasure is in the walking. The trail follows the Supin river past Osla and Seema, villages with intricately carved wooden temples and a living folk tradition that ties them to the Mahabharata. The valley opens gradually until Swargarohini fills the head of it. Add a day and you can push to Jaundhar Glacier or the alpine lake at Marinda Tal.
bestSeason: March to June, September to November

itinerary.description: Drive into the Govind sanctuary and settle at the roadhead village.

itinerary.title: Sankri to Puani Garaat

itinerary.title: Puani Garaat to Kalkattiyadhaar
itinerary.description: Past Osla village and its wooden temple, climbing above the Supin gorge.

itinerary.title: Kalkattiyadhaar to Har Ki Dun and back
itinerary.description: The valley floor opens under Swargarohini; a long day out and back to the meadow head.

itinerary.title: Kalkattiyadhaar to Puani Garaat
itinerary.description: Retrace the gorge trail with the valley behind you.

itinerary.title: Puani Garaat to Sankri
itinerary.description: Walk out to Taluka and drive back to Sankri.
