title: Harihar Fort Trek
shortDescription: Eighty rock-cut steps at close to eighty degrees — the most photographed staircase in the Sahyadri.
description: Harihar, also called Harshagad, is a small fort near Trimbakeshwar whose approach is famous out of all proportion to its size: a flight of roughly eighty steps carved directly into a near-vertical rock face, with shallow handholds cut beside them. The exposure is real and the rock gets slick in the rain. The summit plateau holds a water cistern, a small Hanuman shrine and views across the Trimbak range. Not for anyone uneasy with heights.

itinerary.title: Nirgudpada to Harihar Fort and back
itinerary.description: A short approach walk, the vertical rock staircase to the plateau, and the descent by the same route.

title: Harishchandragad Trek
shortDescription: The Konkan Kada overhang, a rock-cut Shiva temple and a 6th-century hill fort in one trek.
description: Harishchandragad is the most storied fort in the Sahyadri, with origins in the 6th century and a set of features nothing else in the range can match: the Konkan Kada, a concave 1,800-foot cliff that curves inward like a cobra hood; the Kedareshwar cave with a giant shivling standing in waist-deep water; and the Harishchandreshwar temple carved from a single rock. Routes climb from Khireshwar, Pachnai and Nalichi Vaat, the last of which is a technical gully requiring ropes.

itinerary.title: Khireshwar to Harishchandragad plateau
itinerary.description: Climb through Tolar Khind to the plateau, visit the Kedareshwar cave and temple, and camp near the Konkan Kada.

itinerary.title: Sunrise at Konkan Kada, descend via Pachnai
itinerary.description: Watch the sunrise over the cliff, then take the easier Pachnai route down.

title: Indrahar Pass Trek
shortDescription: Over the Dhauladhar crest from Kangra into the Chamba valley, on an old shepherd route.
description: Indrahar is the traditional Gaddi shepherd crossing over the Dhauladhar, climbing from Triund past Lahesh Cave to a 14,245 ft notch in the ridge. It is a steep, rocky trek with a boulder-strewn summit day, and the view from the pass takes in the Pir Panjal to the north and the entire Kangra plain to the south. Most groups return the same way; the full traverse continues down to Chamba.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October

itinerary.title: Dharamkot to Triund
itinerary.description: Climb the standard Triund trail to the ridge camp.

itinerary.title: Triund to Lahesh Cave
itinerary.description: Past Snowline and the Laka glacier to a rock shelter below the pass.

itinerary.title: Lahesh Cave to Indrahar Pass and back
itinerary.description: A steep boulder climb to the notch with views into Chamba, then back down.

itinerary.title: Lahesh Cave to Triund
itinerary.description: Retrace the glacier trail to the ridge.

itinerary.title: Triund to Dharamkot
itinerary.description: Descend to McLeod Ganj.

title: Irshalgad Trek
shortDescription: A sharp pinnacle above the Mumbai-Pune expressway, with a rock needle at the top.
description: Irshalgad is a small fort on a distinctive twin-horned hill visible from the expressway, topped by a rock needle called the Irshal pinnacle that requires technical climbing to summit — most trekkers stop at the plateau and the Nedhe rock window below it. The climb from Morbe is short but the final section is exposed. Note that a landslide devastated Irshalwadi village on this hillside in 2023; check current trail status and access with local authorities.

itinerary.title: Morbe to Irshalgad plateau and back
itinerary.description: Climb through scrub and rock to the plateau and the Nedhe window below the pinnacle, then descend.

title: Japfu Peak Trek
shortDescription: Nagaland's second-highest peak, with the world's tallest recorded rhododendron on its slopes.
description: Japfu rises to 9,890 ft just south of Kohima and is usually climbed for the sunrise, when the ranges of Nagaland and Manipur show through the mist below. Its slopes hold a rhododendron arboreum recorded in the Guinness Book at over 100 feet — the tallest of its kind. The climb is short but steep and can be muddy; it is often combined with Dzukou Valley in a single trip.

itinerary.title: Kohima to Kigwema, trek to base camp
itinerary.description: Drive to the trailhead and climb to a forest camp below the summit.

itinerary.title: Summit and return to Kohima
itinerary.description: A pre-dawn climb to the peak for sunrise, then descend and drive back.

title: Kalavantin Durg Trek
shortDescription: A pinnacle with steps cut into its side and no railing anywhere on them.
description: Kalavantin Durg is a freestanding rock pinnacle beside Prabalgad, and the last stretch to its flat top is a flight of steps hewn into the rock with a sheer drop on the open side and nothing to hold. It is short — a couple of hours from Prabalmachi — but genuinely exposed, and it becomes dangerous in rain or wind when the rock is slick. Clear-weather ascents give a fine view over Matheran, Karnala and Irshalgad.

itinerary.title: Thakurwadi to Kalavantin Durg and back
itinerary.description: Climb to Prabalmachi, then take the exposed rock-cut staircase to the pinnacle top before descending.

title: Kalsubai Peak Trek
shortDescription: The highest point in Maharashtra, climbed by iron ladders to a temple on the summit.
description: At 5,400 ft Kalsubai is the tallest peak in Maharashtra, and the climb from Bari village is short, steep and interrupted by four sets of iron ladders bolted to the rock. A small temple to the goddess Kalsubai stands on the summit. From the top the view takes in Alang, Madan, Kulang, Ratangad and the Bhandardara reservoir. Monsoon turns the trail into a stream and the whole hillside green; winter gives the clearest views.

itinerary.title: Bari Village to Kalsubai summit and back
itinerary.description: A steep three-hour climb with four ladder sections to the summit temple, then the descent.

title: Kanamo Peak Trek
shortDescription: A non-technical 19,553 ft summit above Kibber in Spiti — one of the highest walk-up peaks in India.
description: Kanamo is remarkable for how high it goes without ever requiring technical climbing. Starting from Kibber, one of the highest inhabited villages in the world, the route is a sustained walk on scree and rock to a summit at 19,553 ft with views over the Parang La, the Kunzum range and deep into Ladakh. What makes it hard is the altitude, not the terrain — the trek is built around several acclimatisation days in Kaza and Kibber before the summit push.

itinerary.title: Manali to Kaza
itinerary.description: Drive over Kunzum La into Spiti.

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation in Kaza
itinerary.description: A rest day with short walks to Key monastery.

itinerary.title: Kaza to Kibber
itinerary.description: Move base to Kibber and walk towards the Chicham bridge.

itinerary.title: Kibber to Kanamo Base
itinerary.description: A steady scree climb to the base camp on the mountain's shoulder.

itinerary.title: Base to Kanamo summit and back to Kibber
itinerary.description: A long, thin-air walk to the summit and a full descent to the village.

itinerary.title: Buffer and exploration day
itinerary.description: A reserve day for weather, or for visiting Langza and Komic.

itinerary.title: Kibber to Manali
itinerary.description: Return drive over Kunzum La.

title: Kareri Lake Trek
shortDescription: A shallow, snow-fed lake below the Dhauladhar, clear enough to see the bed across it.
description: Kareri Lake is a freshwater lake at 9,650 ft fed by melting snow from the Dhauladhar ridge above, and it is shallow enough that the bottom is visible across most of its width. The trail from Kareri village follows the Nyund stream through pine and rhododendron, with a small Shiva temple on the far bank of the lake. It is a straightforward two- or three-day trek and a good alternative to the crowds at Triund.
bestSeason: April to June, September to November

itinerary.title: Dharamshala to Kareri Village, trek to Reoti
itinerary.description: Drive to the base village and walk up the Nyund stream to a forest camp.

itinerary.title: Reoti to Kareri Lake and back to Kareri Village
itinerary.description: Climb to the lake and its Shiva shrine, then descend the full trail.

itinerary.title: Kareri Village to Dharamshala
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Kashmir Great Lakes Trek
shortDescription: Seven alpine lakes and four passes across the meadows of the Kashmir Himalaya.
description: Widely regarded as the most beautiful trek in India, Kashmir Great Lakes strings together Vishansar, Krishansar, Gadsar, Satsar, Gangabal and Nundkol across seven days of walking. The pattern repeats and never gets old: climb a pass, drop into a bowl holding a lake the colour of glass, camp in a meadow, repeat. The grass is greener and the flowers denser than almost anywhere else in the Himalaya, and the whole route stays above 11,000 ft.

itinerary.title: Srinagar to Sonamarg
itinerary.description: Drive to the base town and acclimatise.

itinerary.title: Sonamarg to Nichnai
itinerary.description: A steep climb through the Shekdur maple forest into an open valley.

itinerary.title: Nichnai to Vishansar
itinerary.description: Cross Nichnai Pass and drop to the twin lakes of Vishansar and Krishansar.

itinerary.title: Vishansar to Gadsar
itinerary.description: Over Gadsar Pass, the highest point, to a lake ringed with wildflowers.

itinerary.title: Gadsar to Satsar
itinerary.description: An army check post and a chain of seven small interlinked lakes.

itinerary.title: Satsar to Gangabal
itinerary.description: Over Zaj Pass on a boulder trail to the twin lakes below Harmukh.

itinerary.title: Gangabal to Naranag
itinerary.description: A long descent through birch forest to the ancient temple complex at Naranag.

itinerary.title: Naranag to Srinagar
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Kedarkantha Trek
shortDescription: A gentle winter summit in the Govind sanctuary, with a 360-degree Himalayan skyline from the top.
description: Kedarkantha is the trek most Indian trekkers cut their teeth on, and for good reason. The trail climbs steadily through dense pine and oak out of Sankri, opens into wide snow clearings, and finishes with a short, exhilarating push to a 12,500 ft summit. From the top the horizon fills with Swargarohini, Bandarpoonch and Black Peak. Snow lies deep between December and March, which is when the trek is at its most striking, though the same route is a green meadow walk through spring and autumn.
bestSeason: December to April, September to November

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Sankri
itinerary.description: A long mountain drive along the Tons river valley into the Govind Pashu Vihar sanctuary, ending at the roadhead village of Sankri.

itinerary.title: Sankri to Juda Ka Talab
itinerary.description: The first climb, through thick pine forest, to a frozen forest pond ringed by camping clearings.

itinerary.title: Juda Ka Talab to Kedarkantha Base
itinerary.description: The forest thins into open snow meadows with the first clear view of the summit cone ahead.

itinerary.title: Base to Summit and down to Hargaon
itinerary.description: A pre-dawn start for the summit ridge, then a long descent past Hargaon's shepherd huts.

itinerary.title: Hargaon to Sankri
itinerary.description: A steady forest descent back to the roadhead.

itinerary.title: Sankri to Dehradun
itinerary.description: Return drive to Dehradun.

title: Kedartal Trek
shortDescription: A glacial lake at 15,000 ft with Thalay Sagar rising straight out of it.
description: Kedartal is short in distance and hard in every other way. The trail out of Gangotri traverses loose scree and exposed rock ledges above the Kedar Ganga for three days, with very little easy ground. What waits at the end is one of the most dramatic campsites in Garhwal: an emerald lake at 15,000 ft with Thalay Sagar, Bhrigupanth and Jogin standing over it. The exposure and the loose terrain make this unsuitable as an early trek.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Uttarkashi
itinerary.description: Drive along the Bhagirathi.

itinerary.title: Uttarkashi to Gangotri
itinerary.description: Continue to Gangotri and acclimatise.

itinerary.title: Gangotri to Bhoj Kharak
itinerary.description: A steep scree traverse above the Kedar Ganga into a birch grove.

itinerary.title: Bhoj Kharak to Kedar Kharak
itinerary.description: More loose traversing ground with Thalay Sagar coming into view.

itinerary.title: Kedar Kharak to Kedartal and back
itinerary.description: A boulder-field push to the lake and its Thalay Sagar reflection.

itinerary.title: Kedar Kharak to Gangotri
itinerary.description: The full descent back along the exposed traverse.

itinerary.title: Gangotri to Dehradun
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Khaliya Top Trek
shortDescription: A short Kumaon meadow climb with Panchachuli, Nanda Devi and Nanda Kot in one sweep.
description: Khaliya Top is a bugyal above Munsiyari that gives an unusually complete Kumaon panorama for very little effort: Panchachuli's five peaks, Nanda Devi, Nanda Kot and Rajrambha all from one ridge. The climb from Balati Farm is short and mostly through rhododendron forest, and the meadow carries heavy snow from December to March, making it one of the better winter treks in Kumaon.
bestSeason: December to April, September to November

itinerary.title: Kathgodam to Munsiyari
itinerary.description: A long drive through Kumaon to the hill town below Panchachuli.

itinerary.title: Balati Farm to Khaliya Top and back
itinerary.description: Climb through rhododendron into the meadow for the full Kumaon panorama.

itinerary.title: Munsiyari to Kathgodam
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Kheerganga Trek
shortDescription: A short forest climb in the Parvati valley to natural hot springs at 9,700 ft.
description: Kheerganga is the easiest well-known trek in the Parvati valley and the one most people do first. The trail from Barsheni follows the river past Rudra Nag waterfall and climbs steadily through pine forest to a meadow with hot sulphur springs and a small Shiva shrine. It can be done as an overnight, and it stays open through much of the year, though the upper section holds snow in winter.
bestSeason: March to June, September to November

itinerary.title: Barsheni to Kheerganga
itinerary.description: Follow the Parvati past Rudra Nag falls and climb through forest to the hot springs meadow.

itinerary.title: Kheerganga to Barsheni
itinerary.description: Descend by the Nakthan village trail.

title: Kodachadri Trek
shortDescription: A sunset peak above the Mookambika reserve, with an iron pillar and a stone temple on top.
description: Kodachadri rises behind the Mookambika temple at Kollur, inside a wildlife sanctuary of dense evergreen forest. The trail from Nittur or Karakatte climbs through the forest to open grassland and the Sarvajna Peetha, a small stone shrine associated with Adi Shankaracharya, beside an iron pillar of uncertain age. The Hidlumane waterfall is on the longer route. It faces west, which makes the sunset from the summit its main draw.

itinerary.title: Nittur to Kodachadri via Hidlumane Falls
itinerary.description: Climb through evergreen forest past the waterfall to the grassland summit and the Sarvajna Peetha shrine.

itinerary.title: Sunrise and descent to Nittur
itinerary.description: Morning views over the Ghats, then descend by the forest trail.

title: Kolahoi Glacier Trek
shortDescription: To the foot of Kashmir's largest glacier, below the peak they call the Goddess of Light.
description: The Kolahoi glacier feeds the Lidder river and sits below Kolahoi peak, at 17,799 ft the highest mountain in the Kashmir valley. The trek from Aru follows the same early stages as Tarsar Marsar to Lidderwat, then turns up the Satlanjan valley to the glacier snout. It is a short trek with a serious mountain at the end of it, and the glacier's visible retreat over recent decades makes it a sobering one.

itinerary.title: Srinagar to Aru
itinerary.description: Drive through Pahalgam to the base village.

itinerary.title: Aru to Lidderwat
itinerary.description: Walk the Lidder trail through pine and meadow.

itinerary.title: Lidderwat to Satlanjan
itinerary.description: Turn up the side valley into open grazing grounds.

itinerary.title: Satlanjan to Kolahoi Glacier and back to Lidderwat
itinerary.description: A moraine walk to the glacier snout below Kolahoi peak, then descend.

itinerary.title: Lidderwat to Aru and Srinagar
itinerary.description: Walk out and return drive.

title: Kolli Hills Trek
shortDescription: Seventy hairpin bends, a thousand-step waterfall and a millet-farming plateau in the Eastern Ghats.
description: The Kolli Hills rise from the Namakkal plains through a road of seventy hairpin bends to a plateau of millet fields, jackfruit and coffee, long associated in Tamil literature with medicinal herbs and, in folklore, with mountain spirits. The Agaya Gangai waterfall is reached by around a thousand stone steps down a gorge — and back up again. Walking routes link the Arappaleeswarar temple, the viewpoints and the hill villages.

itinerary.title: Semmedu to Agaya Gangai falls and back
itinerary.description: Descend the thousand steps to the waterfall and climb back up to the plateau.

itinerary.title: Plateau villages and viewpoints
itinerary.description: Walk between the millet fields, the Arappaleeswarar temple and the escarpment viewpoints.

title: Kolukkumalai Trek
shortDescription: Sunrise from the world's highest tea estate, on the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border.
description: Kolukkumalai is generally described as the highest tea estate in the world, its bushes planted on slopes at around 7,900 ft above Munnar on the Tamil Nadu side of the border. The estate still runs an old-fashioned orthodox tea factory. Most visits are timed for sunrise from the summit ridge, when the plains of Tamil Nadu appear below a layer of cloud. The trek from Suryanelli is short but the jeep track up is famously rough.

itinerary.title: Suryanelli to Kolukkumalai summit
itinerary.description: A pre-dawn climb through the tea slopes to the ridge for sunrise over the Tamil Nadu plains, then a walk through the estate and factory.

title: Kuari Pass Trek
shortDescription: Curzon's old Himalayan viewpoint trail, facing the Nanda Devi sanctuary wall head-on.
description: Walked and popularised by Lord Curzon in 1905, the Kuari Pass trail is still one of the finest viewpoints in the Indian Himalaya. The pass looks directly across at Nanda Devi, Dronagiri, Kamet and Hathi-Ghoda, and the approach through Gulling and Khullara is a long forest-and-meadow walk that stays interesting throughout. It works both as a spring green trek and as a deep-snow winter one, and Pangarchulla Peak extends it for anyone who wants a summit.
bestSeason: December to April, September to November

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Joshimath
itinerary.description: Drive up the Alaknanda valley to Joshimath.

itinerary.title: Joshimath to Gulling
itinerary.description: Drive to Dhak and climb through terraced fields and forest to the Gulling clearing.

itinerary.title: Gulling to Khullara
itinerary.description: A steady forest climb that breaks out into a meadow facing the Dronagiri massif.

itinerary.title: Khullara to Kuari Pass and down to Tali
itinerary.description: The pass day, with the full Nanda Devi sanctuary wall opening up at the top.

itinerary.title: Tali to Auli and drive to Joshimath
itinerary.description: Down through the Gorson meadows to the Auli ski slopes.

itinerary.title: Joshimath to Rishikesh
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Kudremukh Trek
shortDescription: The horse-face peak — rolling shola grassland and a ridge walk to Karnataka's third-highest summit.
description: Kudremukh takes its name from the horse-face profile of the peak seen from one side, and the trek to it is a long, undulating walk through shola grassland inside a national park. From the forest office at Mullodi the trail crosses streams, passes the Ontimara tree and climbs a series of ridges to a 6,207 ft summit with views over the Ghats to the coast. Guides are mandatory, numbers are capped, and the turnaround time is strictly enforced.

itinerary.title: Mullodi to Kudremukh peak and back
itinerary.description: A long day from the forest office across streams and grassland ridges to the summit, with a mandatory early turnaround for the descent.

title: Kumara Parvatha Trek
shortDescription: South India's toughest one-day climb, with three false summits before the real one.
description: Kumara Parvatha, also called Pushpagiri, is the benchmark hard trek of the Western Ghats: a relentless climb from Kukke Subramanya through Bhattaru Mane and Kallu Mantapa, over Shesha Parvatha and two more false summits before the actual top at 5,617 ft. Roughly 22 km round trip with over 4,000 ft of gain, leeches through the wet season, and very little shade on the upper grassland. Forest department permits are required and entry timings are enforced.

itinerary.title: Kukke Subramanya to Bhattaru Mane
itinerary.description: A steep forest climb to the traditional homestay and forest check post below Shesha Parvatha.

itinerary.title: Summit push and descent
itinerary.description: Over Shesha Parvatha and the false summits to Kumara Parvatha, then the full descent to Kukke.

title: Kumbhalgarh Fort Trail Trek
shortDescription: Walking beside the second-longest continuous wall in the world, through the Aravalli forest.
description: Kumbhalgarh's perimeter wall runs for roughly 36 kilometres along the Aravalli ridges, widely described as the longest continuous wall after the Great Wall of China, enclosing hundreds of temples and the birthplace of Maharana Pratap. The trek follows sections of the wall and the surrounding wildlife sanctuary, where leopard, wolf and sloth bear are present. Cool-season walking through dry deciduous forest with long views across Rajasthan.

itinerary.title: Kumbhalgarh Fort and the wall
itinerary.description: Explore the fort and walk a stretch of the perimeter wall along the ridge.

itinerary.title: Sanctuary forest to Thandi Beri
itinerary.description: Walk through the wildlife sanctuary's dry forest and waterholes.

itinerary.title: Thandi Beri to Ghanerao
itinerary.description: Descend the Aravalli slopes to the village and its Jain temples.

title: Kunti Betta Trek
shortDescription: Twin rocky hillocks near Pandavapura, an easy night trek with a Mahabharata story attached.
description: Kunti Betta is a pair of low granite hills near Pandavapura, named in local tradition for Kunti of the Mahabharata, whose sons are said to have sheltered here. The climb is short and rocky with some boulder scrambling near the top, and the summit looks over paddy fields, sugarcane and the Thonnur lake. It is commonly done as an overnight or night trek from Bangalore or Mysore.

itinerary.title: Pandavapura to Kunti Betta and back
itinerary.description: A short rocky climb with boulder sections to the twin summits, then the descent.

title: Lohagad Fort Trek
shortDescription: Four gateways and the scorpion-tail spur, on the easiest big-name fort in the Sahyadri.
description: Lohagad is a UNESCO-listed Maratha fort and the most beginner-friendly of the Lonavala group — steps most of the way, four successive gateways still standing, and the Vinchu Kata or scorpion's tail, a narrow fortified spur that juts out from the main plateau. It was used by Shivaji to store treasury. The monsoon view from the spur, with cloud pouring through the gap towards Visapur, is the reason to go.

itinerary.title: Lohagadwadi to Lohagad and back
itinerary.description: Climb the stepped path through the four gateways, walk out onto Vinchu Kata, and return.

title: Lonar Crater Lake Trek
shortDescription: A walk around and into a meteorite crater formed in basalt around 50,000 years ago.
description: Lonar is the only known hypervelocity impact crater in basalt rock, formed roughly 50,000 years ago, with a saline and alkaline lake at the bottom that supports unusual microbial life — and which turned pink in 2020 when its salinity shifted. The rim circuit is about six kilometres and passes a set of Chalukya-era temples on the way down to the water. It is a wildlife sanctuary, so entry rules apply.

itinerary.title: Crater rim circuit and descent to the lake
itinerary.description: Walk the rim, descend past the Chalukya temples to the lake shore, and climb back out.

title: Madhugiri Fort Trek
shortDescription: A steep monolith climb with iron handrails on the exposed upper slabs.
description: Madhugiri is often described as Asia's second-largest monolith, and the fort climb up it is steeper and more exposed than Savandurga's, with sections where the granite tilts to a gradient that needed iron railings drilled in. The trail passes through several fortified gateways to a summit with a small temple and a wide view over the Tumkur plains. It should be avoided in rain and in the middle of a hot day.

itinerary.title: Madhugiri Town to fort summit and back
itinerary.description: Climb through the fortified gateways and up the railed granite slabs to the summit temple, then descend.

title: Madmaheshwar Trek
shortDescription: The second Panch Kedar temple, in a valley below Chaukhamba.
description: Madmaheshwar is where the navel of Shiva is worshipped, the second of the Panch Kedar, set in a green valley at 11,470 ft with Chaukhamba filling the head of it. The walk from Ransi through Gaundhar and Bantoli is a river-valley trail through forest and terraced fields, moderate throughout, and the meadow at Budha Madmaheshwar above the temple gives the best mountain views. Popular with pilgrims through summer and autumn.
bestSeason: May to June, September to November

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Ransi
itinerary.description: Drive up the Mandakini valley to the trailhead village.

itinerary.title: Ransi to Bantoli
itinerary.description: Descend to the river confluence through Gaundhar village.

itinerary.title: Bantoli to Madmaheshwar and Budha Madmaheshwar
itinerary.description: A steady climb to the temple and the meadow above it for the Chaukhamba view.

itinerary.title: Madmaheshwar to Ransi and Rishikesh
itinerary.description: Descend to the roadhead and return.

title: Mahabaleshwar Range Trek
shortDescription: A multi-day plateau traverse above the Konkan, linking Arthur's Seat, Chandragad and the Koyna valley.
description: The Mahabaleshwar plateau is the largest in the Sahyadri, and traversing its rim rather than driving between its viewpoints turns it into a proper multi-day trek. The route strings together Arthur's Seat, the Chandragad ridge, dense evergreen forest on the Koyna side and long stretches of cliff edge looking down 3,000 ft into the Konkan. It works in winter and post-monsoon; the strawberry fields and mist of the hill station are a soft landing at the end.

itinerary.title: Mahabaleshwar to Arthur's Seat ridge
itinerary.description: Walk the plateau rim past the viewpoints to a camp on the cliff edge.

itinerary.title: Arthur's Seat to Chandragad
itinerary.description: Descend the ridge into forest and climb to the Chandragad fort plateau.

itinerary.title: Chandragad to the roadhead
itinerary.description: A final descent through the Konkan-facing forest.

title: Makalidurga Trek
shortDescription: A railway-track approach to a small hilltop fort with a lake below it.
description: Makalidurga is a compact hill fort about an hour north of Bangalore, and the walk in follows a stretch of railway line before turning up the rocky hillside past a Shiva temple. The summit holds the remains of the fort wall and a Nandi statue, with the Makalidurga lake spread out below. It is short enough for a half day and one of the more pleasant easy treks near the city.

itinerary.title: Makalidurga Station to summit and back
itinerary.description: Follow the track and climb the rocky trail past the temple to the fort ruins, returning by the same route.

title: Markha Valley Trek
shortDescription: Ladakh's classic teahouse trek — two high passes, gorges, monasteries and homestays.
description: Markha Valley is the best-known trek in Ladakh and one of the few in India that can be walked entirely on homestays. The route crosses Ganda La and Kongmaru La, drops through the Markha gorge with its river crossings, and passes the monasteries at Skiu and Hankar and the ruins of Techa. The landscape is Tibetan-plateau dry, coloured in ochre and purple, with Kang Yatse standing over the upper valley.

itinerary.title: Arrive Leh
itinerary.description: Arrive and rest for altitude.

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation in Leh
itinerary.description: Short walks to Shanti Stupa and Leh Palace.

itinerary.title: Leh to Chilling, trek to Skiu
itinerary.description: Drive along the Indus and walk into the mouth of the Markha valley.

itinerary.title: Skiu to Markha
itinerary.description: A long gorge walk with river crossings between poplar-shaded villages.

itinerary.title: Markha to Hankar
itinerary.description: Past the Techa monastery ruins perched on a cliff above the trail.

itinerary.title: Hankar to Nimaling
itinerary.description: Climb onto the high grazing plateau below Kang Yatse.

itinerary.title: Nimaling to Shang Sumdo via Kongmaru La
itinerary.description: The high pass and a long descent through a narrow coloured gorge.

itinerary.title: Shang Sumdo to Leh
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Meesapulimala Trek
shortDescription: The second-highest peak in South India, across eight hills of shola and rhododendron.
description: Meesapulimala stands at 8,661 ft in the Western Ghats above Munnar, second in South India only to Anamudi. The trek from Rhodo Valley crosses eight successive hills through pockets of shola forest, tea gardens and grassland, with Nilgiri tahr often visible on the slopes. Kerala Forest Development Corporation manages access and the trek is booked through them, usually with a night at the Rhodo Valley camp.

itinerary.title: Munnar to Rhodo Valley camp
itinerary.description: Drive through the tea estates to the base camp and walk the surrounding grassland in the afternoon.

itinerary.title: Rhodo Valley to Meesapulimala and back
itinerary.description: Cross the chain of eight hills to the summit and return to the camp and Munnar.

title: Milam Glacier Trek
shortDescription: An old Indo-Tibetan trade route up the Johar valley to a large Kumaon glacier.
description: The Milam trail follows the Gori Ganga up the Johar valley on what was, until 1962, a working trade route to Tibet. The gorge sections are dramatic and in places carved into the cliff, and the abandoned stone village of Milam at the top — once home to hundreds of trading families — is a striking place to reach. The glacier lies a short walk beyond. Inner Line Permits are required for the upper valley.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October

itinerary.title: Kathgodam to Munsiyari
itinerary.description: A long drive to the Johar valley trailhead town.

itinerary.title: Munsiyari to Lilam
itinerary.description: Drive to Selapani and walk along the Gori Ganga.

itinerary.title: Lilam to Bogudiyar
itinerary.description: Through the narrow gorge on a cliff-cut trail.

itinerary.title: Bogudiyar to Rilkot
itinerary.description: Continue up the valley past waterfalls and rock overhangs.

itinerary.title: Rilkot to Burfu
itinerary.description: The valley widens with the first Johar villages.

itinerary.title: Burfu to Milam Village
itinerary.description: Reach the abandoned stone trading village below the glacier.

itinerary.title: Milam Glacier and back
itinerary.description: Walk to the glacier snout and return to the village.

itinerary.title: Milam to Rilkot
itinerary.description: Begin the descent down the valley.

itinerary.title: Rilkot to Bogudiyar
itinerary.description: Continue through the gorge.

itinerary.title: Bogudiyar to Munsiyari
itinerary.description: Walk out to Lilam and drive to Munsiyari.

title: Mount Kilimanjaro Trek
shortDescription: Africa's highest point at 19,341 ft, and the tallest freestanding mountain in the world.
description: Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa and the tallest freestanding mountain on earth, climbed without technical equipment by several routes — Machame, Lemosho, Marangu and Rongai among them. The walk passes through five distinct climate zones in a few days, from rainforest through moorland and alpine desert to the glaciers at Uhuru Peak. Success depends almost entirely on acclimatisation, which is why longer routes have far better summit rates.
bestSeason: January to March, June to October

itinerary.title: Machame Gate to Machame Camp
itinerary.description: Climb through montane rainforest to the first camp.

itinerary.title: Machame to Shira Camp
itinerary.description: Out of the forest onto the moorland of the Shira plateau.

itinerary.title: Shira to Barranco via Lava Tower
itinerary.description: A climb-high sleep-low day to the Lava Tower and down to Barranco.

itinerary.title: Barranco to Karanga
itinerary.description: Scramble the Barranco Wall and traverse to the Karanga valley.

itinerary.title: Karanga to Barafu
itinerary.description: Cross alpine desert to the summit camp.

itinerary.title: Barafu to Uhuru Peak and down to Mweka
itinerary.description: A midnight start to Stella Point and the summit, then a long descent.

itinerary.title: Mweka Camp to Mweka Gate
itinerary.description: Descend through the rainforest to the park gate.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.description: Transfer to Moshi or Arusha.

title: Mount Rinjani Trek
shortDescription: An active volcano on Lombok with a crescent crater lake and a cone inside it.
description: Rinjani is the second-highest volcano in Indonesia at 12,224 ft, and its caldera holds Segara Anak, a crescent-shaped lake with the still-active Barujari cone rising from the water and hot springs on the shore. The climb from Sembalun crosses long open savannah before a punishing ash-and-scree summit push in the dark. It is a national park with a permit system, and the mountain closes during the rainy season and after volcanic activity.

itinerary.title: Sembalun to Crater Rim
itinerary.description: Cross the savannah and climb the long ridge to the rim camp.

itinerary.title: Summit push and descent to Segara Anak
itinerary.description: A pre-dawn scree climb to the summit, then down to the crater lake and hot springs.

itinerary.title: Segara Anak to Senaru Rim
itinerary.description: Climb out of the caldera to the western rim camp.

itinerary.title: Senaru Rim to Senaru village
itinerary.description: Descend through tropical forest to the park gate.

title: Mullayanagiri Trek
shortDescription: The highest peak in Karnataka, above the coffee estates of Chikkamagaluru.
description: Mullayanagiri is the tallest point in Karnataka at 6,330 ft and the easiest of the state's big peaks to reach — a road runs almost to the base of the summit steps. The proper trek approaches from Sarpadhari or Baba Budangiri instead, following the ridge across open grassland with the Bhadra valley on one side and coffee estates on the other. A small Shiva shrine sits on the summit. Mist and wind are near-constant on the ridge.

itinerary.title: Sarpadhari to Mullayanagiri summit
itinerary.description: A ridge walk across open grassland from the Sarpadhari trailhead to the summit shrine, returning by the same route or the road.

title: Nafran Valley Trek
shortDescription: A hidden hanging valley off the Sindh, thick with wildflowers and almost no other trekkers.
description: Nafran is a broad, flower-filled valley reached from the Sindh side of the Kashmir Himalaya, and its appeal is precisely that it has stayed off the standard circuit. The trek walks through birch forest and Gujjar settlements into a valley floor that in July turns almost entirely purple and yellow with bloom, ringed by unnamed peaks. It is moderate walking with a genuinely remote feel.

itinerary.title: Srinagar to Kulan
itinerary.description: Drive up the Sindh valley towards Sonamarg.

itinerary.title: Kulan to Shitkadi
itinerary.description: Walk into the side valley through birch and pine.

itinerary.title: Shitkadi to Nafran
itinerary.description: Climb into the hanging valley and its flower meadows.

itinerary.title: Nafran exploration day
itinerary.description: Walk to the head of the valley and the ridge above it.

itinerary.title: Nafran to Shitkadi
itinerary.description: Retrace the trail down the valley.

itinerary.title: Shitkadi to Kulan and Srinagar
itinerary.description: Walk out and return drive.

title: Nag Tibba Trek
shortDescription: The classic Himalayan weekend trek — one night out, a real summit, and a big view.
description: Nag Tibba is the highest point of the Nag Tibba range at 9,915 ft, and the shortest genuine Himalayan trek accessible from Delhi over a weekend. The trail from Pantwari climbs through oak forest to the serpent-god shrine at Nag Devta, then up a ridge to a summit that looks out at Swargarohini, Bandarpoonch, Kala Nag and Gangotri peaks. It carries light snow in winter and is walkable almost year-round.

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Pantwari, trek to Nag Tibba base
itinerary.description: Morning drive via Mussoorie, then a forest climb to the base camp near the Nag Devta shrine.

itinerary.title: Base to summit and back to Pantwari
itinerary.description: An early ridge climb to the summit, then the full descent and drive back to Dehradun.

title: Nandi Hills Trek
shortDescription: Tipu Sultan's summer hill fort, and the classic first trek for anyone in Bangalore.
description: Nandi Hills is an ancient hill fortress used by Tipu Sultan as a summer retreat, and the stepped trail up from Sultanpet is a short, well-marked climb of about 1,200 steps. At the top are the Bhoganandeeshwara temple complex, Tipu's Drop and the fort walls, plus a view that is famous for early-morning cloud below the ridge. It is heavily visited — going on a weekday and starting before dawn makes a considerable difference.

itinerary.title: Sultanpet to Nandi Hills and back
itinerary.description: Climb the stepped trail to the fort plateau for sunrise, walk the temple complex and viewpoints, then descend.

title: Narasimha Parvatha Trek
shortDescription: The highest point of the Agumbe range, climbed through some of India's wettest rainforest.
description: Narasimha Parvatha is the tallest peak in the Agumbe hills at 5,010 ft, reached through rainforest that receives among the highest rainfall in the country. The trail from Kigga or Agumbe is long and steep, passing the Barkana falls viewpoint before opening onto summit grassland. King cobras are known in this forest, which is a research site for the species. Leeches are unavoidable outside the driest months.

itinerary.title: Kigga to summit area
itinerary.description: A long rainforest climb past the Barkana viewpoint to grassland near the top.

itinerary.title: Descend to Kigga
itinerary.description: The full descent through the forest.

title: Netravati Peak Trek
shortDescription: A grassland ridge in the Charmadi ghats known for sunrise above a sea of cloud.
description: Netravati Peak, sometimes called Ombattu Gudda, sits in the Charmadi range and is best known for mornings when the valleys below fill completely with cloud and the surrounding peaks stand out as islands. The trail from Bangarabalige valley crosses streams and grassland ridges with several steep pulls. It is leech-heavy after rain and the route finding is not obvious, so a local guide is worth having.

itinerary.title: Bangarabalige to Netravati ridge camp
itinerary.description: Cross streams and climb grassland ridges to a camp near the summit.

itinerary.title: Sunrise and descent
itinerary.description: Dawn above the cloud layer, then the descent to the valley.

title: Nilgiris Green Lake Trek
shortDescription: A reservoir walk through the Parsons Valley shola forest above Ooty.
description: Green Lake sits in the Parsons Valley catchment above Ooty, a still reservoir surrounded by dense shola forest that supplies the town's water. Because it is a protected catchment, entry is regulated by the forest department and permits with a guide are required; the trek walks through eucalyptus and shola stands with a good chance of seeing gaur and sambar. Quiet, cool and completely different from the tourist Ooty a few kilometres away.

itinerary.title: Ooty to Green Lake and back
itinerary.description: A guided walk through the Parsons Valley catchment forest to the reservoir and back.

title: Nokrek National Park Trek
shortDescription: The highest peak in the Garo hills, inside a UNESCO biosphere reserve of wild citrus.
description: Nokrek is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in the Garo Hills, protecting the wild citrus species Citrus indica — regarded as an ancestor of cultivated oranges — along with hoolock gibbon and red panda populations. The trek to the 4,652 ft summit runs through thick tropical forest from Daribokgre village. It is humid, leech-prone in the wet months, and about as far from Himalayan trekking as the country offers.

itinerary.title: Tura to Daribokgre, trek towards Nokrek summit
itinerary.description: Drive to the village on the park boundary and climb through tropical forest to a camp near the summit ridge.

itinerary.title: Descend to Daribokgre and drive to Tura
itinerary.description: Return through the biosphere reserve forest.

title: Nongriat Double Decker Root Bridge Trek
shortDescription: Three thousand steps down a gorge to a bridge grown, not built, from living fig roots.
description: The Khasi practice of training Ficus elastica roots across rivers has produced bridges that strengthen with age rather than rotting, and the double-decker at Nongriat is the most famous of them. Reaching it means descending roughly 3,000 stone steps from Tyrna into the gorge, crossing two steel suspension bridges over the Umshiang, and climbing all of it back out. Rainbow Falls is another hour beyond. Physically demanding despite the short distance.

itinerary.title: Tyrna to Nongriat
itinerary.description: Descend around 3,000 stone steps and cross the suspension bridges to the double-decker root bridge and village homestays.

itinerary.title: Rainbow Falls and climb out to Tyrna
itinerary.description: An optional morning walk to Rainbow Falls, then the long step climb back up.

title: Pachmarhi Satpura Trail Trek
shortDescription: Sandstone gorges, ancient rock shelters and the highest point in Madhya Pradesh.
description: Pachmarhi sits in the Satpura biosphere reserve, a plateau of red sandstone cut by ravines and waterfalls, with rock shelters carrying paintings that go back thousands of years. Trails link Dhupgarh, the highest point in Madhya Pradesh at 4,429 ft, with the Jatashankar and Mahadeo caves and a set of deep pools. Forest permits and guides are needed for the sanctuary sections, and the walking is easy in cool weather.

itinerary.title: Pachmarhi to Dhupgarh
itinerary.description: Walk to the highest point of the state for sunset over the Satpura ranges.

itinerary.title: Jatashankar and the ravine pools
itinerary.description: A day among the sandstone gorges, caves and rock shelters.

itinerary.title: Bee Falls and Apsara Vihar
itinerary.description: A final circuit through the waterfall trails before leaving.

title: Pakshipathalam Trek
shortDescription: Boulder caves in the Brahmagiri sanctuary where rare birds nest among the rocks.
description: Pakshipathalam sits deep in the Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary north of Thirunelli, a jumble of enormous boulders forming caves that shelter a notable variety of birds — the name means the birds' underworld. Reaching it means a steep climb through dense forest with a mandatory forest guide, and the sanctuary holds elephant and gaur. Permits are issued from Thirunelli and numbers are limited.

itinerary.title: Thirunelli to Pakshipathalam and back
itinerary.description: A guided climb through sanctuary forest to the boulder caves and viewpoint, returning the same day.

title: Pangarchulla Peak Trek
shortDescription: A demanding boulder-and-snow summit facing the Nanda Devi sanctuary.
description: Pangarchulla shares its approach with Kuari Pass but diverges into something much harder. The summit day is long — often fourteen hours — over a boulder field that stays snow-covered well into spring, with a final scramble to a 15,069 ft top. The reward is a summit panorama that includes Nanda Devi, Dronagiri, Kamet, Chaukhamba and Neelkanth. It is usually run in April and May when the snow is consolidated.
bestSeason: March to May, September to October

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Joshimath
itinerary.description: Drive up the Alaknanda valley.

itinerary.title: Joshimath to Gulling
itinerary.description: Drive to Dhak and climb to the Gulling clearing.

itinerary.title: Gulling to Khullara
itinerary.description: Forest climb to the meadow camp.

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation at Khullara
itinerary.description: A height-gain walk towards Kuari Pass and back.

itinerary.title: Khullara to Pangarchulla summit and back
itinerary.description: The long summit day across the boulder field and final snow scramble.

itinerary.title: Khullara to Auli and Joshimath
itinerary.description: Descend through the Gorson meadows to Auli.

itinerary.title: Joshimath to Rishikesh
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Parvathamalai Trek
shortDescription: A vertical pilgrimage climb with chain sections to a hilltop Shiva temple.
description: Parvathamalai near Tiruvannamalai is a steep, rocky pilgrimage hill topped by the Mallikarjuna temple, and the final stretch of the climb runs along an exposed rock face where iron chains are fixed for handholds. Pilgrims climb it barefoot, often at night, and the hill has a long association with siddhas and herbal medicine. It is short in distance and genuinely demanding in exposure and gradient.

itinerary.title: Thenmathimangalam to Parvathamalai temple and back
itinerary.description: A steep climb through scrub and rock to the chain section and the hilltop temple, then the descent.

title: Patalkot Gorge Trek
shortDescription: A horseshoe gorge 1,700 feet deep, home to Bharia and Gond villages.
description: Patalkot is a horseshoe-shaped valley in Chhindwara district sunk roughly 1,700 feet below the surrounding plateau, so deep that sunlight reaches parts of the floor only briefly each day. Bharia and Gond communities live in villages inside it and hold a considerable body of herbal knowledge. The trek descends the gorge wall to the Doodhi river and the settlements, then climbs back out — short in distance, steep in both directions.

itinerary.title: Rated to the gorge floor
itinerary.description: Descend the steep gorge wall to the Doodhi river and the villages inside Patalkot.

itinerary.title: Climb out to the plateau
itinerary.description: The steep ascent back to the rim and the viewpoint.

title: Phoktey Dara Trek
shortDescription: A ridge above the Singalila range with a Sleeping Buddha view and almost no crowds.
description: Phoktey Dara is a ridgeline in the Singalila belt near Sombaria, reached through Dhupi forest and the meadow at Bhaley Dhunga. The Kanchenjunga panorama from the top is as complete as Sandakphu's, but the trail sees a fraction of the visitors and passes through villages that are only now developing homestays. Short, moderate and best in spring for the rhododendron or in autumn for clarity.
bestSeason: March to May, October to December

itinerary.title: Bagdogra to Sombaria
itinerary.description: Drive into West Sikkim to the base village.

itinerary.title: Sombaria to Dhupi Dara
itinerary.description: A climb through fir and rhododendron to the first ridge camp.

itinerary.title: Dhupi Dara to Phoktey Dara and back
itinerary.description: The summit ridge with the full Kanchenjunga panorama at sunrise.

itinerary.title: Descend to Sombaria and drive to Bagdogra
itinerary.description: Walk out and return.

title: Phulara Ridge Trek
shortDescription: A rare Indian trek that walks along the crest of a ridge rather than up to it.
description: Most Himalayan treks climb to a viewpoint; Phulara stays on the ridgeline for an entire day, with valleys falling away on both sides and the Bandarpoonch and Swargarohini peaks in view for hours. The route from Sankri goes through Sewa village and the meadow at Bhoj Gadi, then onto the ridge itself. It is short, low-altitude by Garhwal standards and best in spring when the meadow flowers are out.
bestSeason: April to June, September to November

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Sankri
itinerary.description: Drive into the Govind sanctuary.

itinerary.title: Sankri to Sewa
itinerary.description: A gentle forest walk to a village with an old wooden temple.

itinerary.title: Sewa to Bhoj Gadi
itinerary.description: Climb through pine into the meadow below the ridge.

itinerary.title: Bhoj Gadi to Phulara Ridge and down to Dhatmir
itinerary.description: The ridge day, walking the crest with drops on both sides before descending.

itinerary.title: Dhatmir to Sankri and Dehradun
itinerary.description: Walk out and return drive.

title: Pin Bhaba Pass Trek
shortDescription: Kinnaur's green Bhaba valley crossing into Spiti's high desert over a 16,105 ft pass.
description: Pin Bhaba is the shorter, less technical sibling of Pin Parvati and by many accounts the more beautiful of the two. The Kinnaur approach through the Bhaba valley is lush — grass, streams and grazing meadows at Mulling and Karah — and the change on the Spiti side is abrupt and total. The pass day is long with a steep snow section, and the descent to Baldar and Mudh runs through some of the most colourful rock in the Himalaya.
location: Kinnaur to Spiti, Himachal Pradesh, India

itinerary.title: Shimla to Kafnu
itinerary.description: A long drive along the Sutlej into Kinnaur.

itinerary.title: Kafnu to Mulling
itinerary.description: Walk up the Bhaba valley through pine and birch.

itinerary.title: Mulling to Karah
itinerary.description: Into wide grazing meadows with the valley opening out.

itinerary.title: Karah to Phustirang
itinerary.description: Above the treeline to the last camp on the Kinnaur side.

itinerary.title: Phustirang to Pin Bhaba Pass and down to Baldar
itinerary.description: The crossing day, with a steep snow climb and an abrupt change of landscape at the top.

itinerary.title: Baldar to Mudh
itinerary.description: Descend the Pin valley to the roadhead village.

itinerary.title: Mudh to Kaza
itinerary.description: Drive through the Pin Valley National Park to Kaza.

itinerary.title: Kaza to Manali or Shimla
itinerary.description: Return drive out of Spiti.

title: Pin Parvati Pass Trek
shortDescription: One of the hardest classic crossings in India — green Parvati valley over to the desert of Spiti.
description: Pin Parvati is a long, committing traverse from the Parvati valley in Kullu across a 17,457 ft glaciated pass into the Pin valley in Spiti. It runs eleven days, crosses crevassed glacier ground with rope work on the summit day, and involves river crossings that can turn serious in a bad year. The payoff is one of the most complete landscape transitions anywhere: hot springs and dense forest at Kheerganga, then the ochre desert of Spiti. Strictly for experienced trekkers with a competent team.
location: Kullu to Spiti, Himachal Pradesh, India

itinerary.title: Manali to Barsheni
itinerary.description: Drive into the Parvati valley to the roadhead.

itinerary.title: Barsheni to Kheerganga
itinerary.description: A forest climb to the hot springs above the valley.

itinerary.title: Kheerganga to Tunda Bhuj
itinerary.description: Above the treeline into the upper Parvati.

itinerary.title: Tunda Bhuj to Thakur Kuan
itinerary.description: River-side walking with the first serious crossings.

itinerary.title: Thakur Kuan to Odi Thach
itinerary.description: Cross the Parvati on the pandu bridge and continue up the valley.

itinerary.title: Odi Thach to Mantalai Lake
itinerary.description: Reach the source lake of the Parvati, ringed by moraine.

itinerary.title: Mantalai to Base Camp
itinerary.description: A steep moraine climb to the glacier camp below the pass.

itinerary.title: Base Camp to Pin Parvati Pass and down to Pin Valley Camp
itinerary.description: The crossing — roped glacier travel to the pass and a long descent into Spiti.

itinerary.title: Pin Valley Camp to Wichkurung Thatch
itinerary.description: Down the dry Pin valley through changing rock colours.

itinerary.title: Wichkurung Thatch to Mudh
itinerary.description: Walk out to the first village in the Pin valley.

itinerary.title: Mudh to Manali via Kaza
itinerary.description: Long return drive through Spiti.

title: Pindari Glacier Trek
shortDescription: A classic Kumaon valley walk to the glacier snout at Zero Point.
description: The Pindari trek follows the Pindar river up a long Kumaon valley to the glacier's snout, known as Zero Point, with Nanda Kot and Baljuri visible at the head. It is one of the oldest documented trekking routes in India, largely walked on a maintained trail with KMVN rest houses at intervals, which makes it approachable without a full camping setup. The Kafni glacier is a common two-day extension.
bestSeason: April to June, September to October

itinerary.title: Kathgodam to Loharkhet
itinerary.description: Drive through Bageshwar to the trailhead village.

itinerary.title: Loharkhet to Dhakuri
itinerary.description: Climb over the Dhakuri Khal for the first view of the Pindar valley.

itinerary.title: Dhakuri to Khati
itinerary.description: Descend to the largest village in the valley.

itinerary.title: Khati to Dwali
itinerary.description: Walk up the river to the confluence with the Kafni.

itinerary.title: Dwali to Phurkia
itinerary.description: A steeper climb above the treeline.

itinerary.title: Phurkia to Zero Point and back to Dwali
itinerary.description: Reach the glacier snout below Nanda Kot, then descend.

itinerary.title: Dwali to Loharkhet
itinerary.description: The long walk out via Khati and Dhakuri.

title: Pir Panjal Lakes Trek
shortDescription: A lake circuit on the quieter western range, an alternative to the crowded Great Lakes.
description: The Pir Panjal range on the western side of the Kashmir valley holds its own chain of alpine lakes — Nandansar, Kausarnag and others — in high rock basins above the Yusmarg and Aharbal meadows. The trek is comparable in character to Kashmir Great Lakes but sees a small fraction of the traffic, with rougher trails and more boulder ground. Good for anyone who wants Kashmir's lakes without the tent villages.
location: Kulgam and Shopian, Jammu and Kashmir, India

itinerary.title: Srinagar to Aharbal
itinerary.description: Drive to the waterfall town at the base of the range.

itinerary.title: Aharbal to Kungwattan
itinerary.description: Walk through pine forest to a wide meadow.

itinerary.title: Kungwattan to Mahinag
itinerary.description: Climb above the treeline on a shepherd trail.

itinerary.title: Mahinag to Kausarnag
itinerary.description: Reach the largest of the Pir Panjal lakes in its rock bowl.

itinerary.title: Kausarnag to Nandansar
itinerary.description: A boulder traverse over a ridge to a second lake basin.

itinerary.title: Nandansar to Kungwattan
itinerary.description: Descend the far side back into the meadows.

itinerary.title: Kungwattan to Aharbal and Srinagar
itinerary.description: Walk out and return drive.

title: Prashar Lake Trek
shortDescription: A floating island in a hill lake, with a thirteenth-century pagoda temple beside it.
description: Prashar Lake sits at 8,960 ft above the Beas valley near Mandi, with a three-tiered pagoda temple to the sage Prashar on its bank and a small floating island of matted vegetation that shifts position on the water. Its depth has reportedly never been established. The trek from Baggi village is short and gentle, and the ridge above the lake gives a wide view of the Dhauladhar, Pir Panjal and Kinnaur ranges — a good winter weekend option.

itinerary.title: Mandi to Baggi, trek to Prashar Lake
itinerary.description: Drive to the base village and climb through oak forest and meadow to the lake and temple.

itinerary.title: Prashar Lake to Baggi
itinerary.description: Walk the ridge for the Dhauladhar view and descend to the road.

title: Pythalmala Trek
shortDescription: A steep grassland climb on the Kannur-Coorg border with a sheer drop at the top.
description: Pythalmala is a hill on the Kerala-Karnataka boundary near Kannur, reached by a short, steep climb through forest and then a long stretch of open grass ridge. The summit ends abruptly at a cliff edge looking into Coorg, and the wind there is strong enough to be worth respecting. It is a half-day trek, popular locally and still quiet compared to the Wayanad peaks.

itinerary.title: Pythalmala base to summit and back
itinerary.description: A steep forest and grassland climb to the cliff-edge summit on the state border, returning the same way.

title: Rajgad Fort Trek
shortDescription: Shivaji's capital for twenty-six years, spread across three machis and a citadel.
description: Rajgad was the seat of the Maratha kingdom before Raigad, and it remains the most complete hill fort in the Sahyadri: three fortified spurs — Padmavati, Suvela and Sanjeevani machi — radiating from the Balekilla citadel, with bastions, water tanks, palace foundations and kilometres of wall. A full circuit takes a day on its own. The Gunjavane and Pali routes are the usual approaches, and the traverse onward to Torna is a classic Sahyadri outing.

itinerary.title: Gunjavane to Padmavati Machi
itinerary.description: Climb the Chor Darwaja route to the main plateau and camp near the Padmavati temple.

itinerary.title: Fort circuit and descent
itinerary.description: Walk Suvela and Sanjeevani machi and the Balekilla, then descend to the village.

title: Rajmachi Trek
shortDescription: Twin fortresses above the Lonavala valley, best walked at night in the monsoon.
description: Rajmachi is a pair of fortified peaks — Shrivardhan and Manaranjan — with the village of Udhewadi between them, guarding the old Borghat trade route. The 15 km walk in from Lonavala is flat enough that many groups do it as a night trek, arriving for sunrise on the ramparts. In monsoon the trail runs beside waterfalls the whole way and fireflies fill the forest in early June. The Kondana caves lie a short detour off the route.

itinerary.title: Lonavala to Udhewadi
itinerary.description: A long, mostly level walk along the plateau road and trail to the village between the two forts.

itinerary.title: Shrivardhan and Manaranjan, return to Lonavala
itinerary.description: Climb both forts for the Borghat views, then walk back out.

title: Rangaswamy Peak Trek
shortDescription: A sacred pillar of rock in the eastern Nilgiris, revered by the Badaga and Toda communities.
description: Rangaswamy Peak is a distinctive rock pillar in the eastern Nilgiris near Kotagiri, held sacred by the Badaga and Toda communities and associated with a local tradition about the deity Rangaswamy moving here from Karnataka. The trek approaches through tea estates and shola patches to the base of the pillar, with the Moyar gorge and the Sigur plateau visible below. Access is guided and the summit itself is not climbed out of respect.

itinerary.title: Kotagiri to Rangaswamy Peak base and back
itinerary.description: Walk through tea estates and shola to the base of the rock pillar with views over the Moyar gorge, then return.

title: Ranipuram Trek
shortDescription: The Ooty of Kerala — shola grassland and evergreen forest in northern Kasaragod.
description: Ranipuram sits at around 3,600 ft in the hills of Kasaragod, a mosaic of shola forest, monsoon evergreen and open grassland that once carried the name Madathumala. The walk to the summit through the reserve forest is short and mostly gentle, and the view runs across the Kerala-Karnataka border into Coorg. Wild elephants use these forests, so the forest department requires a guide for the upper trail.

itinerary.title: Ranipuram to the summit grassland and back
itinerary.description: A short guided walk through shola and evergreen forest to the open summit and its border views.

title: Ratangad Trek
shortDescription: The jewel fort, with a natural rock window framing the Bhandardara valley.
description: Ratangad is named for the jewel of the Sahyadri, and its defining feature is Nedhe — a natural hole punched clean through the rock near the summit, big enough to walk into, that frames Alang, Madan, Kulang and Kalsubai on one side and the Bhandardara backwaters on the other. The climb from Ratanwadi begins at the 11th-century Amruteshwar temple and includes four ladder sections. Monsoon is spectacular; the boat approach across the reservoir is a good variation.

itinerary.title: Ratanwadi to Ratangad summit
itinerary.description: Visit the Amruteshwar temple, climb the ladder sections to the plateau and camp near the caves.

itinerary.title: Nedhe rock window and descent
itinerary.description: Walk to the natural rock window at sunrise, then descend to the village.

title: Roopkund Trek
shortDescription: The mystery lake of skeletons at 16,000 ft, reached across the great Bedni and Ali meadows.
description: Roopkund earned its fame from the human remains scattered around a small glacial tarn at 16,000 ft, dated to roughly the 9th century and still not fully explained. The trek to it is a classic in its own right, crossing the enormous twin meadows of Ali and Bedni Bugyal with Trishul and Nanda Ghunti standing over them, then climbing steep scree to the lake. Note that access to the lake itself has been restricted by the Uttarakhand High Court on ecological grounds; check the current status before planning.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Lohajung
itinerary.description: A long drive into the Nanda Devi outer sanctuary region.

itinerary.title: Lohajung to Didna
itinerary.description: Down to the Neel Ganga and up the far side to a hillside village.

itinerary.title: Didna to Ali Bugyal
itinerary.description: A forest climb that ends abruptly at the edge of one of India's largest high meadows.

itinerary.title: Ali Bugyal to Patar Nachauni
itinerary.description: A rolling meadow traverse to Bedni Bugyal and on to the last grazing ground.

itinerary.title: Patar Nachauni to Bhagwabasa
itinerary.description: A steep switchback climb past the Kalu Vinayak shrine onto the rock shelf below the lake.

itinerary.title: Bhagwabasa to Roopkund and down to Patar Nachauni
itinerary.description: An early scree climb to the lake and Junargali ridge, then a long descent.

itinerary.title: Patar Nachauni to Wan
itinerary.description: Back across Bedni and down through the Wan forest.

itinerary.title: Lohajung to Rishikesh
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Rudranath Trek
shortDescription: The hardest of the Panch Kedar to reach — a rock temple in a high meadow bowl.
description: Rudranath is the fourth of the Panch Kedar temples, where Shiva is worshipped in the form of a face, and it is the most difficult of the five to walk to. The trail from Sagar climbs through dense forest to the Panar bugyal and then across a long series of meadows and ridges to a small stone shrine set in a rock hollow. The Nanda Devi, Trishul and Hathi-Ghoda peaks are in view for much of the walk.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Sagar
itinerary.description: Drive via Gopeshwar to the trailhead village.

itinerary.title: Sagar to Panar Bugyal
itinerary.description: A long forest climb into the first meadow.

itinerary.title: Panar to Rudranath and back
itinerary.description: Cross the ridges and meadows to the rock temple, returning to camp.

itinerary.title: Panar to Sagar
itinerary.description: Descend the forest trail to the village.

itinerary.title: Sagar to Rishikesh
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Rumtse to Tso Moriri Trek
shortDescription: A high-plateau traverse across Rupshu, over five passes, ending at a great salt lake.
description: This is a walk across the Changthang plateau, where the average camp is above 15,000 ft and the horizon is enormous and almost empty. The route crosses five passes including Yalung Nyau La and Kyamayuri La, passes the Tso Kar salt lake and Changpa nomad camps with their pashmina herds, and ends at Tso Moriri's deep blue expanse. Altitude, not gradient, is the difficulty here — thorough acclimatisation in Leh is essential.

itinerary.description: Arrive and rest.

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation in Leh
itinerary.description: Short walks and permit formalities.

itinerary.description: Over Kyamar La and Mandalchan La onto the plateau.

itinerary.description: Walk along the salt flats among Changpa nomad camps.

itinerary.description: Over Horlam Kongka La on open plateau ground.

itinerary.description: The highest pass of the trek, then the first sight of Tso Moriri below.

itinerary.title: Korzok to Leh
itinerary.description: Long return drive along the lake and the Indus.

title: Rupin Pass Trek
shortDescription: A trail that changes character every single day, finishing up a hanging snow gully.
description: Rupin Pass is the trek people cite when they argue that variety matters more than altitude. It begins in Uttarakhand at Dhaula and ends in Himachal at Sangla, and in between it passes a hanging village at Jhaka, a three-stage waterfall you climb alongside, snow bridges over the Rupin, and a final gully to a 15,250 ft pass. The descent into the Sangla valley through Ronti Gad is as good as the climb.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October
location: Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand to Kinnaur, Himachal Pradesh, India

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Dhaula
itinerary.description: Drive to the roadhead on the Rupin river.

itinerary.title: Dhaula to Sewa
itinerary.description: A river-level walk to a village with a distinctive Kinnauri-style temple.

itinerary.title: Sewa to Jiskun
itinerary.description: Cross into Himachal and climb to a village stacked on the hillside.

itinerary.title: Jiskun to Saruwas Thach
itinerary.description: Past the hanging village of Jhaka into pine and rhododendron forest.

itinerary.title: Saruwas Thach to Dhanderas Thach
itinerary.description: Cross snow bridges into the wide meadow facing the three-stage waterfall.

itinerary.title: Dhanderas Thach to Upper Waterfall Camp
itinerary.description: Climb alongside the waterfall to the camp above it.

itinerary.title: Upper Waterfall to Rupin Pass and down to Ronti Gad
itinerary.description: The gully climb to the pass and a long descent into the Sangla side.

itinerary.title: Ronti Gad to Sangla
itinerary.description: Descend to the Baspa valley roadhead.

title: Saddle Peak Trek
shortDescription: The highest point in the Andamans, climbed through tropical rainforest from Diglipur.
description: Saddle Peak is the tallest point in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands at 2,418 ft, inside a national park in North Andaman near Diglipur. The trail from Lamiya Bay climbs through dense tropical evergreen forest — buttressed trees, lianas, and a soundtrack of hornbills and cicadas — to a summit ridge with views over the sea on both sides. Forest department permits are required and the humidity is relentless.
location: North Andaman, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, India

itinerary.title: Lamiya Bay to Saddle Peak and back
itinerary.description: A humid rainforest climb to the highest point in the islands, returning to the coast the same day.

title: Salher Fort Trek
shortDescription: The highest fort in Maharashtra, and the site of the Marathas' first open-field victory.
description: Salher rises to 5,141 ft in the Baglan range near the Gujarat border, making it the highest fort in Maharashtra and the second-highest peak in the state after Kalsubai. The Battle of Salher in 1672 was the first pitched-battle victory the Marathas won against the Mughals in open ground. The climb from Waghambe passes carved gateways and cisterns to a broad summit with a Parshuram temple. Often paired with the neighbouring Salota fort.

itinerary.title: Waghambe to Salher summit
itinerary.description: Climb through the fortified gateways to the summit plateau and camp near the Parshuram temple.

itinerary.title: Salota and descent
itinerary.description: An optional climb of neighbouring Salota, then descend to the village.

title: Sandakphu Phalut Trek
shortDescription: The only trail in India where Everest and Kanchenjunga are visible in the same frame.
description: The Singalila ridge runs along the India-Nepal border, and from Sandakphu at 11,930 ft you can see four of the world's five highest peaks — Everest, Lhotse, Makalu and Kanchenjunga — with the Kanchenjunga massif arranged in the shape locals call the Sleeping Buddha. The trek walks the ridge from Sepi through Tumling and Sandakphu to Phalut, staying in teahouses, crossing back and forth between the two countries. Spring brings the rhododendron and magnolia bloom.
bestSeason: March to May, October to December

itinerary.title: NJP to Sepi
itinerary.description: Drive through Darjeeling's tea country to the base village.

itinerary.title: Sepi to Tumling
itinerary.description: Climb through Singalila National Park forest to a ridge village in Nepal.

itinerary.title: Tumling to Kalipokhri
itinerary.description: Ridge walking past Gairibas and Kaiyakatta with the border underfoot.

itinerary.title: Kalipokhri to Sandakphu
itinerary.description: The steep Bikeybhanjang climb to the highest point in West Bengal.

itinerary.title: Sandakphu to Phalut
itinerary.description: A long, exposed ridge traverse with Kanchenjunga alongside all day.

itinerary.title: Phalut to Gorkhey and Srikhola
itinerary.description: Drop off the ridge into a forested valley and a stream-side village.

itinerary.title: Srikhola to NJP
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Sar Pass Trek
shortDescription: A Parvati valley pass known for its long glissade down the far side.
description: Sar Pass is a Kasol-based trek through the villages and forests above the Parvati valley, and it has a signature moment: on the far side of the 13,800 ft pass a long snow slope lets you slide most of the way down. The route passes Grahan village, the meadow at Min Thach and the tree line camp at Nagaru, and stays in dense deodar forest for much of its length. It is a popular first Himalayan trek in May and June.
bestSeason: April to June, September to October

itinerary.title: Kasol to Grahan
itinerary.description: A forest walk along the Grahan nala to an old wooden village.

itinerary.title: Grahan to Min Thach
itinerary.description: A steep climb through deodar to a meadow with valley views.

itinerary.title: Min Thach to Nagaru
itinerary.description: A short but hard climb to the exposed ridge camp.

itinerary.title: Nagaru to Sar Pass and down to Biskeri Thach
itinerary.description: The pass crossing, followed by the long snow glissade to the meadow below.

itinerary.title: Biskeri Thach to Barsheni
itinerary.description: Descend through forest to the Parvati roadhead.

title: Sathuragiri Hills Trek
shortDescription: A forest pilgrimage to the Sundaramahalingam temple, open on fixed days each month.
description: Sathuragiri is a hill in the Western Ghats near Watrap whose Sundaramahalingam temple draws pilgrims on new moon and full moon days, when the forest route is officially opened. The climb from Thaniparai runs about six kilometres through reserve forest with waterfalls and herb-rich undergrowth long associated with siddha medicine. Outside the permitted days the trail is closed, and the forest holds elephants.
bestSeason: October to March, on permitted temple days

itinerary.title: Thaniparai to Sathuragiri temple and back
itinerary.description: A forest climb past waterfalls to the Sundaramahalingam temple on a permitted day, returning before the gate closes.

title: Satopanth Tal Trek
shortDescription: A triangular glacial lake above Badrinath, held in legend to be bathed in by the trinity.
description: Satopanth Tal is a near-perfect triangular lake at around 15,100 ft beyond Mana, the last village before the Tibet border. Tradition assigns one corner each to Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh. The route passes the Vasudhara falls and crosses the Chakratirth moraine, with Neelkanth, Chaukhamba and Balakun standing over the whole approach. It is a serious high-altitude trek on rough glacier moraine with no shelter.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Badrinath
itinerary.description: Drive up the Alaknanda to the temple town.

itinerary.title: Badrinath to Laxmi Van
itinerary.description: Walk through Mana and past the Vasudhara falls into a birch grove.

itinerary.title: Laxmi Van to Chakratirth
itinerary.description: Cross moraine and boulder ground below Balakun.

itinerary.title: Chakratirth to Satopanth Tal and back
itinerary.description: Reach the triangular lake on the glacier shelf, then return.

itinerary.title: Chakratirth to Badrinath
itinerary.description: The long descent past Vasudhara to the town.

itinerary.title: Badrinath to Rishikesh
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Savandurga Trek
shortDescription: One of Asia's largest monolithic rock hills, climbed directly up the bare granite.
description: Savandurga is a single enormous granite dome — often described as among the largest monoliths in Asia — split into Karigudda and Billigudda, the black and white hills. The climb up Billigudda goes straight over open rock with painted arrows for guidance and no shade at all, which makes grip and heat the two real hazards. A Nandi shrine sits at the top with views over the Arkavathi and Manchanabele reservoir.

itinerary.title: Savandurga Village to Billigudda summit and back
itinerary.description: A direct climb over open granite to the Nandi shrine at the top, returning the same way before the rock heats up.

title: Sham Valley Trek
shortDescription: The baby trek of Ladakh — low passes, apricot villages and homestays all the way.
description: Sham Valley is the gentlest introduction to Ladakhi trekking, running between the villages of Likir, Yangthang, Hemis Shukpachan and Temisgam on a series of low passes. Nights are spent in village homestays rather than tents, the daily distances are short, and the altitude stays manageable, which makes it workable for families and for anyone with only a few days. Apricot orchards, gompas and stupas line most of the route.

itinerary.title: Arrive Leh
itinerary.description: Arrive and acclimatise.

itinerary.title: Leh to Likir, trek to Yangthang
itinerary.description: Drive to Likir monastery and walk over Phobe La and Charatse La.

itinerary.title: Yangthang to Hemis Shukpachan
itinerary.description: Over Tsermangchen La to a village known for its juniper grove.

itinerary.title: Hemis Shukpachan to Temisgam
itinerary.description: Cross Mebtak La and Bongbong La down to the apricot village.

itinerary.title: Temisgam to Leh
itinerary.description: Return drive along the Indus.

title: Sinhagad Fort Trek
shortDescription: Pune's weekend fort — a short climb to the site of Tanaji Malusare's last battle.
description: Sinhagad is the fort every Pune trekker starts on: an hour's drive from the city, a well-worn hour-long climb, and a plateau full of history — the Kalyan and Pune Darwaja gates, Rajaram's samadhi and the memorial to Tanaji Malusare, who died taking it in 1670. It is busy at weekends and the summit stalls sell pithla bhakri and curd. Best walked early on a monsoon morning when the cloud sits on the ramparts.

itinerary.title: Atkarwadi to Sinhagad and back
itinerary.description: A stepped one-hour climb to the fort gates, a walk around the ramparts and memorials, and the descent.

title: Skandagiri Trek
shortDescription: Bangalore's night trek — a pre-dawn climb to watch sunrise break over a cloud layer.
description: Skandagiri, or Kalavara Durga, is a ruined fort hill north of Bangalore that became famous for night treks timed to reach the summit before sunrise, when the valleys below are often filled with cloud. The climb is about four kilometres of rocky trail past the fort ruins and a Shiva temple. Access has been regulated by the forest department at various times with permits and restrictions on night entry, so check current rules before planning.

itinerary.title: Papagni Mutt to Skandagiri summit and back
itinerary.description: A pre-dawn rocky climb past the fort ruins to the summit for sunrise, then the descent in daylight.

title: Srikhand Mahadev Trek
shortDescription: A punishing pilgrimage climb to a 75-foot natural shivling at 18,570 ft.
description: Srikhand Mahadev is one of the hardest pilgrimage treks in India: roughly 32 km of climbing from Jaon village to a rock formation revered as a shivling, standing about 75 feet high on a summit plateau at 18,570 ft. The route passes Parvati Bagh's wildflower meadows and the boulder field of Bhim Dwar, and the last section crosses loose rock and snow at extreme altitude. It is open only for a short window each July, and the altitude gain per day is severe.

itinerary.title: Shimla to Jaon
itinerary.description: Drive via Rampur and Nirmand to the base village.

itinerary.title: Jaon to Thachru
itinerary.description: A relentless climb past Singhad through dense forest.

itinerary.title: Thachru to Bhim Dwar
itinerary.description: Over Kali Ghati and across Kunsha meadow to the boulder camp.

itinerary.title: Bhim Dwar to Srikhand Mahadev and back
itinerary.description: Through Parvati Bagh and the Nain Sarovar to the shivling plateau, then down.

itinerary.title: Bhim Dwar to Jaon
itinerary.description: The long descent back to the roadhead.

itinerary.title: Jaon to Shimla
itinerary.description: Return drive.

title: Stok Kangri Trek
shortDescription: Ladakh's 20,187 ft trekking peak — currently closed to climbers for ecological recovery.
description: Stok Kangri was for years the most popular non-technical 20,000 ft summit in India, reached over five days from Stok village via Mankarmo and a glacier base camp. Heavy traffic caused severe waste and water problems on the mountain, and the Ladakh authorities and Stok village council closed it from 2020 onward to let the ecosystem recover. It remains closed at the time of writing; check with the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council before planning anything here.
