itinerary.description: Arrive and rest for altitude.

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation in Leh
itinerary.description: Short acclimatisation walks around the town.

itinerary.title: Leh to Stok, trek to Chang Ma
itinerary.description: Drive to Stok village and walk into the gorge.

itinerary.title: Chang Ma to Mankarmo
itinerary.description: Continue up the valley to the last grazing camp.

itinerary.title: Mankarmo to Base Camp
itinerary.description: A short day to the glacier base camp with an afternoon acclimatisation walk.

itinerary.title: Base Camp to summit and back
itinerary.description: A midnight start across the glacier and up the summit ridge, returning the same day.

itinerary.title: Base Camp to Stok and Leh
itinerary.description: Descend the full valley and drive back.

itinerary.title: Buffer day
itinerary.description: A reserve day for weather.

title: Sunderdhunga Trek
shortDescription: The valley of beautiful stones, ending under the wall of Maiktoli and Tharkot.
description: Sunderdhunga means valley of beautiful stones, and it is the wildest of the three glacier valleys reached from Khati in Kumaon. The trail climbs to Jatoli and then into a hanging valley below the Maiktoli and Tharkot faces, ending at the Sukhram cave and the Baljuri glacier. There is no infrastructure past Jatoli, the river crossings can be difficult, and it sees a fraction of Pindari's traffic.
bestSeason: May to June, September to October

itinerary.title: Kathgodam to Loharkhet
itinerary.description: Drive to the trailhead village.

itinerary.title: Loharkhet to Dhakuri
itinerary.description: Over the Dhakuri Khal into the Pindar valley.

itinerary.title: Dhakuri to Khati
itinerary.description: Descend to the valley's main village.

itinerary.title: Khati to Jatoli
itinerary.description: Turn up the Sunderdhunga valley to the last village.

itinerary.title: Jatoli to Kathaliya
itinerary.description: Enter the wild upper valley with the first big faces in view.

itinerary.title: Kathaliya to Sukhram Cave and Baljuri glacier
itinerary.description: Reach the glacier basin below Maiktoli and Tharkot.

itinerary.title: Kathaliya to Khati
itinerary.description: Descend the valley to the village.

itinerary.title: Khati to Loharkhet
itinerary.description: Walk out via Dhakuri.

title: Surya Top Trek
shortDescription: A quiet Garhwal meadow summit above the Yamuna valley, good in deep winter.
description: Surya Top sits above the Kharsali and Dodital side of the Yamuna valley, reached through oak and deodar forest to a broad meadow ridge with Bandarpoonch, Kalanag and the Gangotri peaks along the skyline. It is a short trek with a proper high point, sees very few groups, and holds reliable snow through the winter months, which is when most people walk it.
bestSeason: December to April, September to November

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Kuwa
itinerary.description: Drive into the Yamuna valley to the base village.

itinerary.title: Kuwa to Dhamni Thatch
itinerary.description: A forest climb through oak and deodar to the first clearing.

itinerary.title: Dhamni Thatch to Bhondiyan
itinerary.description: Out of the treeline onto the lower meadows.

itinerary.title: Bhondiyan to Surya Top and down to Dhamni
itinerary.description: The summit ridge with the Bandarpoonch panorama, then a long descent.

itinerary.title: Dhamni to Kuwa and Dehradun
itinerary.description: Walk out and return drive.

title: Tadiandamol Trek
shortDescription: Coorg's highest peak, climbed past the wooden Nalknad Palace through shola forest.
description: Tadiandamol is the highest point in Kodagu at 5,735 ft, and the trail starts at the 18th-century Nalknad Palace, a low wooden building that was the last refuge of the Kodagu kings. From there it climbs through pockets of shola forest and open grassland to a summit that looks across the Brahmagiri range towards the Arabian Sea on a clear day. Straightforward walking, best in the months just after the monsoon when the grass is still green.

itinerary.title: Nalknad Palace to Tadiandamol and back
itinerary.description: Climb from the palace through shola forest and grassland to the summit, returning on the same trail.

title: Talle Valley Trek
shortDescription: A subtropical wildlife sanctuary above the Apatani plateau, thick with bamboo, fern and silver fir.
description: The Talle Valley Wildlife Sanctuary sits above Ziro in Arunachal Pradesh, and walking into it means moving through several forest types in a day — bamboo, dwarf fern, orchid-hung broadleaf and finally silver fir. The valley floor is boggy and covered in moss. It is one of the wettest, greenest treks in the country, with clouded leopard and Himalayan black bear in the sanctuary and Apatani villages at the trailhead. Inner Line Permits are required.

itinerary.title: Itanagar to Ziro
itinerary.description: Drive to the Apatani plateau and visit the villages.

itinerary.title: Ziro to Pange
itinerary.description: Drive to the sanctuary gate and walk through bamboo and fern forest to the forest rest house.

itinerary.title: Pange to Talle Valley and back
itinerary.description: Cross into silver fir forest and the mossy valley floor, returning to Pange.

itinerary.title: Pange to Ziro
itinerary.description: Walk out and return to Ziro.

title: Tarsar Marsar Trek
shortDescription: Two almond-shaped sister lakes in the Aru valley, camped beside rather than passed by.
description: Tarsar and Marsar are twin alpine lakes separated by a single ridge, and the great pleasure of this trek is that you camp on the shore of Tarsar rather than merely walking past it. The route from Aru runs through Lidderwat's meadows and the Shekwas valley, crosses Tarsar Pass, and finishes above Marsar looking down at it from the ridge. It is shorter and gentler than Kashmir Great Lakes and just as scenic.

itinerary.title: Srinagar to Aru
itinerary.description: Drive through Pahalgam to the base village.

itinerary.title: Aru to Lidderwat
itinerary.description: A gentle walk along the Lidder through pine forest and meadow.

itinerary.title: Lidderwat to Shekwas
itinerary.description: Climb into a wide valley of shepherd huts and grazing grounds.

itinerary.title: Shekwas to Tarsar Lake
itinerary.description: A short day ending on the shore of the first lake.

itinerary.title: Tarsar to Sundersar via Tarsar Pass
itinerary.description: Over the pass to a smaller lake in a boulder basin.

itinerary.title: Sundersar to Marsar viewpoint and down to Homwas
itinerary.description: An early climb to look down at Marsar, then a long descent.

itinerary.title: Homwas to Aru and Srinagar
itinerary.description: Walk out through Lidderwat and drive back.

title: Tholung Kishong Trek
shortDescription: A pilgrimage route to a remote Lepcha monastery and the meadows above it.
description: Tholung monastery sits deep in the Dzongu region of North Sikkim, a Lepcha reserve where outside access is restricted and the pace of life has changed little. Every three years the monastery displays sacred relics, drawing pilgrims from across the region. The trek continues past it to the Kishong meadows and lake, through leech-heavy forest and river gorges. Permits for Dzongu are required in addition to the standard Sikkim permits.
bestSeason: March to May, October to November

itinerary.title: Gangtok to Lingthem
itinerary.description: Drive into the Dzongu Lepcha reserve.

itinerary.title: Lingthem to Tholung Monastery
itinerary.description: A forest walk along the Rungyoung Chu to the monastery.

itinerary.title: Tholung to Sakyong
itinerary.description: Climb steeply above the monastery into rhododendron forest.

itinerary.title: Sakyong to Kishong Lake and back
itinerary.description: Reach the high meadow and lake below the Kanchenjunga ridge.

itinerary.title: Sakyong to Tholung
itinerary.description: Descend the forest trail to the monastery.

itinerary.title: Tholung to Lingthem and Gangtok
itinerary.description: Walk out and return drive.

title: Torna Fort Trek
shortDescription: The first fort Shivaji captured, and the highest in Pune district.
description: Torna, also called Prachandagad, was taken by a sixteen-year-old Shivaji in 1646 and became the foundation of the Maratha kingdom. At 4,603 ft it is the highest fort in Pune district, with the Budhla Machi and Zunjar Machi spurs running off a long summit ridge. The climb from Velhe is steep and continuous. Most trekkers pair it with Rajgad across a two-day ridge traverse.

itinerary.title: Velhe to Torna and back
itinerary.description: A steep continuous climb to the Bini Darwaja and the summit ridge, with the Budhla Machi spur, then descent.

title: Triund Trek
shortDescription: The Dhauladhar balcony above McLeod Ganj — a few hours up, and the whole range in front of you.
description: Triund is a broad grassy ridge at 9,350 ft that sits directly below the Dhauladhar wall, close enough that the rock face fills the sky above the campsite. It is a three to four hour climb from Dharamkot through oak and rhododendron, which makes it the most accessible Himalayan overnight in the country. Sunset and sunrise from the ridge are the reason to stay rather than day-hike it. Snowline Cafe and the Laka glacier extend the walk another hour.
bestSeason: March to June, September to December

itinerary.title: Dharamkot to Triund
itinerary.description: A steady climb through oak forest and the Magic View switchbacks to the ridge.

itinerary.title: Triund to Dharamkot
itinerary.description: Optional morning walk towards Snowline, then descend to McLeod Ganj.

title: Tulian Lake Trek
shortDescription: A steep climb out of Pahalgam to a frozen-edged lake below the Zanskar range.
description: Tulian Lake sits at around 12,500 ft in a rock amphitheatre above Pahalgam, fed by snowmelt and often carrying ice at its edges well into summer. The trek climbs hard from Baisaran through pine forest and the Zargibal meadows to reach it, and the change from soft valley scenery to bare grey rock is abrupt. It can be done in two or three days and is a good short high-altitude option in Kashmir.

itinerary.title: Pahalgam to Baisaran and Zargibal
itinerary.description: Climb through the Baisaran meadow into pine forest and camp above it.

itinerary.title: Zargibal to Tulian Lake and back
itinerary.description: A steep rocky climb to the lake basin, returning to camp.

itinerary.title: Zargibal to Pahalgam
itinerary.description: Descend to the town.

title: Vagamon Meadows Trek
shortDescription: Rolling green hills and pine forest in Idukki, gentle enough for a first trek.
description: Vagamon is a plateau of smooth grass hills, tea gardens and a planted pine forest at around 3,500 ft in Idukki, and walking between its meadows, the Mundakayam ghat viewpoint and Thangal Para is easy, open country. Paragliding operates here in season, and the mist that sits in the valleys through the early morning is the main draw. A good introduction to Kerala's hill walking without permits or difficulty.

itinerary.title: Vagamon meadows and pine forest
itinerary.description: Walk the grass hills, the pine plantation and the Mundakayam ghat viewpoint.

itinerary.title: Thangal Para and Kurisumala
itinerary.description: A morning walk to the rock outcrop and the Kurisumala ridge before heading back.

title: Valley of Flowers Trek
shortDescription: A UNESCO World Heritage valley that turns into a monsoon flowerbed, paired with the high lake at Hemkund.
description: For ten weeks a year the Bhyundar valley becomes something close to unbelievable: hundreds of flowering species, blue poppies and cobra lilies among them, carpeting a glacial valley floor at 12,000 ft. The trek is short and non-technical, built around a base at Ghangaria, from where one day goes into the Valley of Flowers National Park and another climbs steeply to the Sikh shrine and glacial lake at Hemkund Sahib. It only works in monsoon, which means rain, leeches and slick rock alongside the flowers.

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Joshimath
itinerary.description: A full day along the Alaknanda through the five confluences to Joshimath.

itinerary.title: Joshimath to Ghangaria
itinerary.description: Drive to Govindghat, then a well-paved climb along the Pushpawati to the base village.

itinerary.title: Ghangaria to Valley of Flowers and back
itinerary.description: A gentle walk into the national park, where the valley floor opens into flower meadows.

itinerary.title: Ghangaria to Hemkund Sahib and back
itinerary.description: A steep stone-stepped climb to the glacial lake and gurudwara, the high point of the trek.

itinerary.title: Ghangaria to Govindghat and drive to Joshimath
itinerary.description: Descend the paved trail and drive back down the valley.

itinerary.title: Joshimath to Rishikesh
itinerary.description: Return drive along the Alaknanda.

title: Varsey Rhododendron Sanctuary Trek
shortDescription: A short, gentle walk into a sanctuary that turns entirely red and pink in April.
description: Varsey — also spelled Barsey — is a rhododendron sanctuary in West Sikkim where the forest floor and canopy both belong to the same genus, and in April the whole ridge flowers at once. The walk in from Hilley is barely four kilometres on a well-made trail, ending at a trekkers' hut with a Kanchenjunga view. It is one of the easiest Himalayan treks in the country and a good option with children or limited time.
bestSeason: March to May, October to December

itinerary.title: Jorethang to Hilley, trek to Varsey
itinerary.description: Drive to the sanctuary gate and walk the paved forest trail to the trekkers' hut.

itinerary.title: Varsey to Hilley
itinerary.description: Morning views towards Kanchenjunga, then walk out.

title: Vellagavi Trek
shortDescription: A hidden hamlet below Kodaikanal, reachable only on foot through shola forest.
description: Vellagavi is a village of a few dozen houses in the hills below Kodaikanal that has no road to it — everything arrives on foot or by mule down the trail from Vattakanal. The walk descends through shola forest and cliffs past Dolphin's Nose, with the plains of Tamil Nadu visible far below, and continues to Kumbakarai falls for anyone doing the full traverse. Simple homestays operate in the village.

itinerary.title: Vattakanal to Vellagavi
itinerary.description: Descend past Dolphin's Nose through shola forest and cliff trails to the roadless village.

itinerary.title: Vellagavi to Kumbakarai Falls
itinerary.description: Continue down the trail through forest to the falls and the roadhead.

title: Velliangiri Hills Trek
shortDescription: Seven hills climbed barefoot by pilgrims to a Shiva shrine, known as the Kailash of the South.
description: The Velliangiri Hills near Coimbatore are climbed as a pilgrimage over seven successive summits to a shrine at the top, and tradition has most pilgrims making the ascent barefoot. It is a hard walk — steep, rocky, largely unshaded, with limited water — and the hills fall within a reserve forest with seasonal closures. The trail is usually open for a defined season each year, and the view from the seventh hill covers the whole Coimbatore plain.
bestSeason: February to May, subject to forest department opening

itinerary.title: Poondi to the seventh hill and back
itinerary.description: A long, steep climb over seven successive summits to the Shiva shrine, then the full descent in the same day.

title: Visapur Fort Trek
shortDescription: A monsoon staircase-waterfall climb to the larger of the Lohagad-Visapur pair.
description: Visapur stands opposite Lohagad above the Bhaja caves, and it is the higher and more spacious of the two. Its signature is the monsoon approach: a long rock staircase that turns into a shallow waterfall you climb directly through, walled in by cliff on one side. The plateau holds a large water tank, a Hanuman carving and the remains of the fort walls, and the view down to Lohagad's Vinchu Kata spur is the best in the area.

itinerary.title: Bhaje Village to Visapur and back
itinerary.description: Pass the Bhaja caves, climb the waterfall staircase to the plateau, circle the ramparts and descend.

title: Warwan Valley Trek
shortDescription: A remote crossing from Ladakh's Suru valley into one of Kashmir's least-visited valleys.
description: The Warwan trek goes from Panikhar in the Suru valley over the Lonvilad Gali into the Warwan, a valley so isolated that its villages had no road access for most of modern history. The landscape shifts from Ladakhi rock and glacier to Kashmiri forest and terraced fields over a few days. It is a long walk with genuine remoteness — few other groups, limited bail-out options — and one of the best wilderness experiences in the Indian Himalaya.
location: Kargil and Kishtwar, Jammu and Kashmir, India

itinerary.title: Kargil to Panikhar
itinerary.description: Drive into the Suru valley below Nun and Kun.

itinerary.title: Panikhar to Donara
itinerary.description: Walk up the Suru side valley towards the pass.

itinerary.title: Donara to Kaintal
itinerary.description: A moraine climb to the last camp below the Gali.

itinerary.title: Kaintal to Humpet via Lonvilad Gali
itinerary.description: The crossing, over a glaciated pass and down into the Warwan headwaters.

itinerary.title: Humpet to Kanital
itinerary.description: Descend along the Marwah river through changing vegetation.

itinerary.title: Kanital to Basmina
itinerary.description: Reach the first Warwan villages and their terraced fields.

itinerary.title: Basmina to Inshan
itinerary.description: A valley-floor walk between wooden villages.

itinerary.title: Inshan to Sukhnai
itinerary.description: The final walking day out to the roadhead.

itinerary.title: Sukhnai to Srinagar
itinerary.description: A long return drive via Kishtwar or Anantnag.

title: Yelagiri Swamimalai Trek
shortDescription: A short climb to the highest point of a quiet Tamil Nadu hill station.
description: Swamimalai Hill is the high point of Yelagiri at around 4,338 ft, reached by a marked trail of a few kilometres from Mangalam village through eucalyptus and rock. Yelagiri itself is a small, unhurried hill station between Vellore and Tirupattur, with a lake, a herbal farm and paragliding in season. The trek is easy, well-signed and suitable for families or a first outing.

itinerary.title: Mangalam to Swamimalai summit and back
itinerary.description: A marked trail through eucalyptus and rock to the highest point of Yelagiri, returning the same way.
